latest.title: Influence of AI personalization on consumer loyalty in the restaurant business: balance between efficiency and ethics
latest.abstract: The article examines the influence of artificial intelligence-based personalization on the formation of consumer loyalty in the restaurant business. Current trends in the implementation of AI tools, including recommendation systems, dynamic pricing, and loyalty programs, as well as their impact on customer experience, are analyzed. Based on an analysis of empirical data and scholarly publications, key factors determining the effectiveness of AI personalization are identified: relevance of offers, transparency of data use, and preservation of «human» contact. Particular attention is paid to ethical aspects - issues of privacy, risks of dehumanization of service, and manipulative influence on consumer choice. A model for balanced implementation of AI personalization is proposed, taking into account both economic efficiency and ethical constraints. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of applying the proposed recommendations in forming digital transformation strategies for restaurant enterprises.

latest.title: Adaptive omnichannel brand management architecture for light industry enterprises: from brand identity to performance control
latest.abstract: The article substantiates an integrated approach to brand management in light industry enterprises under conditions of digitalization, changing consumer behavior, and increasing fragmentation of interaction channels. Brand management is interpreted as an organizational and functional subsystem that ensures the alignment of strategic positioning, brand identity, communications, digital and physical touchpoints, and analytical control. A three-layer omnichannel brand-management architecture is proposed, comprising the strategic and identity core, the omnichannel interaction layer, and the performance-control layer. The functional content of the system is structured around four interrelated blocks: strategic planning, design, communications, and analytics. Particular attention is paid to the coordination of websites and mobile interfaces, marketplaces, social media, and physical retail within a unified customer journey. The performance-control layer links consumer response, conversion, loyalty, channel efficiency, and economic results, thereby closing the management loop. A recurrent adaptive management cycle is proposed, including diagnosis, identification of structural imbalance, selection of managerial intervention, implementation, measurement, and adjustment. The proposed approach makes it possible to identify structural bottlenecks in brand management and to select differentiated managerial actions aimed at strengthening brand coherence, continuity of customer experience, and market effectiveness.

latest.title: How Does Cognitive Dissonance Explain Why Consumers Justify Expensive Purchases After the Fact (Post-Purchase Rationalization), And What Does This Mean for Return-Policy Design?
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This paper explores the cognitive dissonance theory developed by Leon Festinger (Festinger, 1957) as an answer to explain why consumers in their normal practices justify their high-cost purchases after they make them. This is often referred to as post-purchase rationalization and/or "buyer's remorse management". Based on the social-psychological literature on dissonance reduction, the consumer-behaviour research on post-purchase evaluation (Oliver, 1980; Sweeney, Hausknecht, & Soutar, 2000), and the current literature on retail returns (National Retail Federation & Happy Returns, 2024, 2025), the paper proposes a framework that integrates purchase involvement, decision irreversibility, and self-concept threat with the intensity of post-purchase dissonance and the rationalization strategies consumers use to manage it. The paper then moves on to the implications of this psychology for the firm, that is, the design of return policies. The ease at which a consumer can reverse a purchase decision has a direct effect on the psychological dynamics of dissonance, with lenient return policies making customers more likely to convert to a purchase and causing a window where dissonance can arise as an actual return. The paper utilizes data from the National Retail Federation, Janakiraman, Syrdal, and Freling (2016) meta-analysis of the U.S. retail return literature, and other secondary sources to illustrate that there were an estimated $890 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2024 (16.9% of sales), a slight decrease to estimated $849.9 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2025 (15.8%), and leniency dimensions (e.g. monetary, temporal, effort, scope and exchange) have an asymmetric influence on purchase and return behaviour. Modeling the moral account: a system dynamics framework for brand-induced moral licensing and behavioral rebound in sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchases perceived as virtuous can license compensatory indulgence that erodes some of the benefit. Recent formal work treats licensing as an environmental rebound mechanism in static consumer models; this study contributes the first dynamic stock-and-flow formalization, developed from a recent conceptual framework of brand-induced moral licensing. Methods Four communication pathways (virtue attribution, identity conferral, effort signaling, and absolution framing) feed two moral accounts with opposite mechanics: credits, which deplete when spent, and credentials, which license behavior without being consumed. The model yields closed-form steady states and a licensing-resistance condition on the rebound ratio ρ> (backfire at ρ> 1). Communication parameters were calibrated through a preregistered content analysis of 120 verbatim-archived units from eight sustainable brands, with perfect dual-coder agreement on the reliability subsample; identity internalization was calibrated from a two-country survey of 3,293 adults. The behavioral conversion parameters are literature-anchored or illustrative, so all rebound magnitudes are model-derived, order-of-magnitude results rather than empirical estimates. Results Rebound stays far below backfire: steady-state values span 0.01 to 0.19 across archetypes, preserving 81 to 99% of gross benefit, across 8,000 uncertainty samples and under structural variants allowing credential depletion, sign reversal, and alternative licensing functions. latest.title: Managing consumer behavior through digital marketing strategies: a comprehensive review
latest.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has fundamentally transformed how businesses influence consumer behavior by leveraging tools such as social media, search engine optimization, content marketing, email marketing, and data analytics. This paper provides a comprehensive review of how digital marketing strategies manage consumer behavior, focusing on their impact on consumer engagement, decision-making, and brand loyalty. The purpose of the article is to conduct a comprehensive study of the theoretical and methodological foundations of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities, to systematize contemporary digital marketing strategies, and to identify the mechanisms through which they influence the processes of forming, transforming, and forecasting consumer needs, motivations, and behavioral patterns. The methodological foundation of this study consists of a set of general scientific and specialized methods, the application of which ensures a systematic and comprehensive approach to the study of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities (in particular, methods of analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, systematization, comparative analysis, etc.). By synthesizing insights from literature and empirical studies, the study identifies and systematizes the key digital marketing tools, their applications, and their influence on consumer behavior across diverse contexts. The analysis highlights the role of personalization, social media engagement, and data-driven decision-making in fostering consumer trust and brand loyalty. latest.title: Integrated Marketing Communication for Trust Building: Wuling Motors in Indonesia's Automotive Market
latest.abstract: This study examines how Wuling Motors employs integrated marketing communication (IMC) to build consumer trust and strengthen its market presence in Indonesia's automotive industry despite the long-standing dominance of Japanese brands. A qualitative case study approach was employed using purposive sampling, in-depth interviews, and thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Wuling's market penetration was achieved through trust-building strategies integrating local legitimacy, consumer experience, and adaptive marketing communication. This study contributes to the existing literature on integrated marketing communication, market penetration, and country-of-origin effects by explaining how IMC strategically reconstructs consumer trust and brand legitimacy for an emerging Chinese automotive brand in a market dominated by established Japanese manufacturers. The findings suggest that managers should prioritize integrated marketing communication to build consumer trust and strengthen market penetration, while policymakers should promote policies that support fair competition and innovation in the automotive industry

latest.title: Promoting responsible tourism using generative AI nudges
latest.abstract: Purpose With rapid modernization and globalization, responsible tourism practices at cultural heritage sites are in decline, as many visitors disengage from activities like volunteering, donating or mindful visits. This shift presents a significant challenge for governments, organizations and societies working to promote meaningful interactions with cultural heritage. Encouraging responsible tourism – where visitors respect local cultures while minimizing negative impacts – is crucial. generative artificial intelligence (GAI) offers an emerging avenue for innovative management practices, providing personalized and emotionally resonant digital nudges that can influence visitor engagement. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding which types of nudges are most effective across cultural contexts. This study aims to investigate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven nudges delivered on emotional response and engagement, aiming to foster responsible tourism behaviour. Design/methodology/approach Using a mixed-methods approach, this study adopted a three-stage investigation. Firstly, this study conducted a content analysis gathered from 262 articles via web scrapping which identified five key themes surrounding responsible tourism. Stage two consisted of 25 in-depth interviews, which provided deeper insights on the factors influencing emotional response towards cultural heritage tourism. In stage 3, this study conducted 300 experiments and surveys, focusing on responses to six cultural nudge images representing Indian and UK cultures. Each image was categorized into neutral, positive and negative nudges, capturing participants’ engagement. latest.title: Value Congruity and Modest Fashion Purchase Decisions Among Young Muslim Consumers in Banten, Indonesia
latest.venue: El-Barka Journal of Islamic Economics and Business
latest.abstract: This study examines how value congruity relates to modest fashion purchase decisions alongside religiosity, electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM), Islamic moral identity, and attitude. Research Methods: A cross-sectional online survey in Banten, Indonesia, yielded 101 eligible cases from 206 responses collected from July 31 to September 11, 2026. Participants were aged 17–25, and 99.0% were students. Associations were estimated through path analysis of unit-weighted composite scores with 5,000 paired bootstrap resamples. Results: Religiosity was associated with Islamic moral identity (β = .814), while value congruity was associated with attitude (β = .763) and purchase-decision scores (β = .639); all three p values were below .001. The equations accounted for 66.3%, 76.2%, and 82.2% of the respective in-sample score variance. Other direct paths, interactions, and exploratory indirect effects were not significant. However, CON–KEP HTMT was .920, and shared-method diagnostics raised concerns. Conclusion: Value congruity warrants further investigation, but measurement overlap, the student-dominated sample, and the cross-sectional design prevent a definitive claim that it is a distinct causal driver. The results support further testing of value-aligned communication rather than claims about verified purchasing behavior.

latest.title: Sustainable Green Marketing as a Business Model
latest.venue: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
latest.abstract: This paper seeks to investigate sustainable green marketing as a business model in the African context. Promoting products or services that are eco-friendly is called green marketing. It involves incorporating sustainable principles into various aspects of marketing. Broadly, the sustainable business principles include investing profits in renewable energy, responsible waste disposal practices and avoiding printed materials. Nevertheless, some organisations in the global south are still grappling with the problem of balancing profit with sustainability. Against this backdrop, this paper is guided by three research questions: what are sustainable green marketing practices in the African business context? what are the benefits of sustainable green marketing to business? and which challenges are faced in implementing sustainable green marketing? Eventually, this study’s results would proffer a business model which can be a key driver of innovation and competitiveness and assist corporate organisations reap substantial economic benefits. Furthermore, green marketing can raise awareness among consumers about the importance of sustainability and environmental impact of their purchasing decisions. An integrative literature review methodology was employed by the authors to understand sustainable green marketing benefits and challenges. The study is guided by two key theories: stakeholder theory and institutional theory. The research findings indicated a deficiency in knowledge, skills, and proficiency in environmental sustainability, conservation, and eco-friendly practices within certain African businesses. Additionally, it was found that certain harmful products were still being used because individuals were unaware of the negative impact these products had on the environment

latest.title: Perceived Accuracy and Relevance of AI-Based Product Recommendations and Generation X Purchase Decisions in Jakarta
latest.abstract: This study examines how perceived accuracy and contextual relevance of artificial-intelligence-based product recommendations influence purchase decisions among Generation X e-commerce users in Jakarta. A quantitative explanatory design was modeled with 300 respondent profiles and 18 reflective indicators. Partial least squares structural equation modeling, 10,000-resample bootstrapping, coefficient-difference testing, and tenfold cross-validation were applied. Perceived accuracy had a stronger positive effect on purchase decisions (β=.604, p<.001) than relevance (β=.217, p<.001), and the difference was significant (Δβ=.387, p<.001). The model explained 54.2% of purchase-decision variance and showed positive Qpredict2​ values. The findings indicate an accuracy–relevance asymmetry: relevance attracts attention, whereas perceived accuracy more strongly reinforces purchase decisions.

latest.title: Consumer financial behavior, digital payments, and financial debt during ritualized consumption
latest.abstract: Ritualized consumption combines emotional engagement, digital purchasing, and financial debt, yet these dynamics remain underexplored in crisis-affected economies. This study examines how Christmas shopping routines, gift-selection practices, and online payment methods are associated with Christmas spirit and Christmas debt among Lebanese consumers. The framework integrates Ritual Theory, Gift-Giving and Social Exchange theories, Normative Social Influence Theory, Hedonic Consumption Theory, and Self-Control Theory. Online survey data from a sample of 284 Lebanese consumers were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Christmas shopping routines showed the strongest association with Christmas spirit (β = 0.472, p < 0.001), while shopping routines and Christmas spirit showed the strongest associations with Christmas debt (both β = 0.380, p < 0.001). Christmas spirit significantly mediated the associations between all three antecedents and Christmas debt, supporting partial mediation. The findings indicate that ritualized, relational, and technologically enabled consumption practices are associated with both positive festive engagement and greater Christmas-related financial obligations. The study contributes to consumer behavior, consumer finance, and digital consumption research by integrating cultural, emotional, technological, and financial perspectives. It offers implications for retailers, policymakers, and digital payment providers seeking to promote responsible spending and financial transparency during high-consumption periods.

latest.title: Investigation of restaurant customers’ behavioral intentions with goal-directed behavior theory
latest.abstract: Behavioral intentions are critical determinants of customer loyalty and competitive advantage in the highly competitive restaurant sector. Understanding these intentions requires an integrated view of psychological, emotional, and cognitive processes, combining motivational theory with memory-related mechanisms in gastronomic decision-making. Existing studies often overlook the dynamic interplay between attitudes, social influences, anticipated emotions, perceived control, past experiences, and cognitive recall in shaping restaurant choices. This three-wave longitudinal study applies the Model of Goal-Directed Behavior (MGB) to a sample of 386 restaurant customers in Istanbul, Türkiye, incorporating memory as a novel moderating variable to illuminate cognitive dimensions of consumer choice. Structural Equation Modeling results showed positive associations of perceived behavioral control, positive anticipated emotions, attitudes, subjective norms, and frequency of past behavior with desire. Desire and frequency of past behavior were positively associated with behavioral intentions, whereas the direct association between perceived behavioral control and intentions was not statistically significant. Memory moderation received differing levels of support across the examined pathways: the interaction involving past behavior was positive and statistically significant, whereas evidence for the desire intention interaction was borderline. The interaction involving perceived behavioral control was not statistically significant. Negative anticipated emotions were not significantly associated with desire in this sample. latest.title: Too crowded to be adventurous: the effect of social crowding on consumer switching behavior
latest.abstract: Introduction Global urbanization has inevitably increased the density of individuals in public spaces, exerting considerable influence on marketing strategies and consumers. Despite expanding research on how consumers are influenced by social crowding, consensus among researchers remains elusive. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this research investigates how social crowding affects consumer switching behavior. Methods Across five studies, including a quasi-experimental field study, we examine the effect of social crowding on switching intentions and test risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway, as well as shared consumption and crowding aversiveness as boundary conditions. Results Social crowding significantly decreases switching intentions, with η 2 ranging from 0.03 to 0.16. Mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway. Importantly, this effect disappears when consumers engage in shared consumption or when the crowding is non-aversive. Discussion These findings offer a resource-based interpretation of consumer responses to crowding. From the COR perspective, maintaining familiar choices may serve a protective function when crowding is appraised as a threat to valued resources. Practically, managers can mitigate the negative effect of crowding on switching behavior by encouraging shared consumption and providing risk-reducing cues.

latest.title: The Effect of Instagram Social Media Marketing and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of H'zhazu MSME Products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Science and Application
latest.abstract: Social media marketing and product quality are important considerations in consumer purchasing decisions, particularly for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating in competitive markets. However, further empirical investigation is needed to understand how these factors are associated with purchasing decisions in the context of traditional-snack MSMEs. This study examines the individual and joint associations of Instagram social media marketing and product quality with purchase decisions among consumers of H'Zhazu MSME products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang. A quantitative cross-sectional design with an associative approach was employed. The study population comprised 348 consumers, from which 78 respondents were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 29. The results revealed that Instagram social media marketing had a positive and statistically significant association with purchase decisions (B = 0.512; β = 0.437; t = 4.103; p < 0.001). Product quality also demonstrated a positive and statistically significant association (B = 0.541; β = 0.465; t = 4.371; p < 0.001). Furthermore, the regression model was statistically significant (F = 110.734; p < 0.001), with an R² of 0.747, indicating that the two predictors jointly accounted for 74.7% of the observed variation in purchase decisions within the sample. This study contributes context-specific empirical evidence concerning the relationship between digital marketing and product quality in a traditional-snack MSME. latest.title: The Emerging Strategies for Longevity, Succession, and Sustainability of Rural Family-Owned Retail Businesses (RFORBs) in Developing Countries
latest.venue: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
latest.abstract: Despite a growing body of literature on family business, succession, and intergenerational transition challenges, few studies have addressed the same family businesses in a rural-sector context. Yet, they play critical socio-economic roles- enhancing social integration, serving as commercial hubs that supply essential goods and services, and supporting vulnerable households, including facilitating trade in the most remote market. The study investigates emerging strategies for business endurance and sustainability in rural retail family enterprises in developing economies. A PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of 27 journal papers focusing on developing countries was conducted, and a thematic synthesis was conducted alongside a bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer version 1.6.20, focusing on keyword analysis, thematic mapping, and clustering to identify emerging themes in rural family-owned businesses transitioning to long-term survival across generations. The findings uncovered key emerging innovation strategies: digitalisation, financial inclusion, and consumer-oriented innovation that enhances resilience and long-term sustainability. Also, the study concludes that vision trap, entrepreneurial traits, occult beliefs or supernatural power, resource availability and capacity are the major barriers to longevity of rural family-owned retail businesses. The study recommends government policy reforms that prioritise the accessibility of digital infrastructure, such as digital devices and networks, as well as financial inclusion. Along with pro-green-energy policy reforms, to enhance the affordability of solar energy- solar Photovoltaic (PV) schemes, to advance digital transformation and improve service provision in remote areas.

latest.title: Modernizing Tradition: How Packaging Creativity and Consumer Curiosity Shape Purchase Intention for Traditional Snacks – A Moderated Mediation Model
latest.abstract: Producers of traditional snacks in emerging markets must modernize their packaging without eroding the authenticity that defines their products. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework and the theory of reasoned action (TRA), this study examines how packaging creativity shapes consumer attitude and purchase intention, and whether consumer curiosity conditions this process. Data were collected through an online survey of 255 Indonesian consumers who evaluated the modernized packaging of Gethuk Anyar, a traditional cassava snack from Ngawi, East Java, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Packaging creativity was positively associated with attitude (β = 0.551) and purchase intention (β = 0.273). Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention (β = 0.610) and partially mediated the creativity–intention relationship (indirect effect = 0.336). Curiosity strengthened the creativity–attitude link (β = 0.170), and the index of moderated mediation was significant (0.103, p = 0.030), indicating a stronger attitudinal pathway among more curious consumers. The model explained 26.9% of the variance in attitude and 60.2% in purchase intention. The findings suggest that micro, small and medium-sized enterprises can combine novelty with culturally relevant cues in packaging and use curiosity-evoking communication to convert visual attention into purchase intention.

latest.title: BLENDED LEARNING MANAGEMENT DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
latest.abstract: This study used a qualitative approach with descriptive method. Data were collected through observation in the madrasah environment, interviews with teachers and madrasah head, and review of learning documents. The analysis was conducted through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing to obtain a complete picture of the practice of Blended Learning in both institutions. The results show that both madrasas have done careful planning by adjusting the curriculum and providing supporting facilities for online learning, such as internet networks and digital devices. In its implementation, MAN 1 Pangandaran applies a shift system between offline and online learning alternately every day, while MAS YPP Jamanis Parigi mostly applies full face-to-face learning with additional online activities according to teacher needs. In the evaluation stage, both implement web-based assessment to ensure objectivity and efficiency of the assessment process. Overall, the implementation of Blended Learning has proven to be an adaptive and effective solution in maintaining the quality of madrasah learning amidst the limitations of the pandemic, as well as showing the flexibility of educational institutions in dealing with dynamic learning system changes.

latest.title: GREEN PARADOX IN CREATIVE RURAL TOURISM: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND PILOT SCALE ASSESSMENT
latest.venue: International Journal of Global Accounting Management Education and Entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: Creative rural tourism destinations increasingly promote green practices to attract eco-conscious travelers, yet tourists do not always respond positively. This study addresses this phenomenon, termed the “green paradox”, by developing a conceptual framework integrating the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, the Theory of Consumption Values, and Attribution Theory. The proposed model positions perceived authenticity as the stimulus that generates green perceived value, which influences revisit intention through two competing pathways: a positive pathway mediated by green satisfaction (via intrinsic attribution) and a negative pathway mediated by green skepticism (via extrinsic attribution). Eight propositions specify the relationships among five constructs. The study extends S-O-R from single mediation to a competing mediation architecture accommodating opposing evaluative processes within the organism stage. A pilot study (n = 97) using PLS-SEM via SmartPLS 3 confirms satisfactory psychometric properties for all 21 measurement items contextualized for Vietnamese creative rural tourism, with outer loadings ranging from 0.834 to 0.909, reliability coefficients exceeding 0.70, AVE values above 0.738, and discriminant validity established through both the Fornell-Larcker criterion and HTMT ratios. The validated scales provide a foundation for subsequent large-scale empirical testing of the proposed framework.

latest.title: Webrooming, Showrooming & Situational Channel Use In Herbal Cosmetics Evidence from Indian Consumers
latest.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study is designed to explore the webrooming, showrooming, situational channel switching of herbal cosmetic products as well as to understand the motives for cross channel shopping. Design/methodology/approach: A cross-sectional survey generated 812 responses. Of these, 578 responses were deemed eligible and complete and thus were retained. For primary channel choice, the measures of webrooming and showrooming were directly measured by asking why they select the channel and the reasons were analysed descriptively. The key proportions were estimated by the use of 95% confidence intervals. Qualitative results were complemented with a thematic analysis of the 561 openended, nonscored responses, using a dictionary. Findings: Webrooming was reported by 48.4% of respondents (95% CI [44.4%, 52.5%]), whereas showrooming was reported by 32.2% (95% CI [28.5%, 36.1%]). When asked to choose their primary channel, 66.4% responded with a channel via both online and offline, and/or a conditional channel, with 33.6% choosing an exclusive online or offline main channel. Quality and effectiveness, reviews and recommendations, ingredients and safety, trust and brand reputation, and convenience and availability were the most frequently identified considerations. The integrated evidence is consistent with digital touchpoints supporting information search and social validation, while stores support sensory inspection and interpersonal assurance. Research limitations/implications: The cross-sectional, non-probability design supports estimation and contextual interpretation, not causal inference. latest.title: Green Brand Equity, Claim Type, and the Credibility Route to Green Advertising Effectiveness
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how green brand equity (GBE) and the benefit emphasized in a green ad claim jointly influence the effectiveness of green advertising on consumer‐based brand equity (CBBE) in the automotive market. Grounded in legitimacy theory and the consumption value framework, a 2 (GBE: high vs. low) × 5 (claim type: neutral, ecological, economic, hedonic, social) experiment was conducted on 807 French car owners, with consumer‐based brand equity measured before and after ad exposure. The main results show that exposure to green advertising improves CBBE of the advertised brand. Additionally, two moderation effects occur. First, ecological claims outperform neutral, economic, and hedonic claims but do not differ from social claims, suggesting that identity‐relevant benefits, rather than ecological content specifically, drive advertising effectiveness. Second, ad exposure is more effective when a brand has high rather than low initial GBE. In addition, a mediation analysis identifies ad credibility as the mechanism through which GBE moderates advertising effectiveness, offering managers guidance on aligning claim design with a brand's existing environmental legitimacy.

latest.title: The Mediating Role of Consumer Satisfaction in The Influence of Trust and Service Quality on Streetwear Purchase Decisions on Shopee
latest.abstract: Background: The rapid expansion of digital marketplaces has heightened the significance of consumer trust, service quality, and satisfaction in determining online purchase decisions, especially among Generation Z buyers who acquire streetwear products via Shopee. Objective: This research investigates the direct influence of consumer trust and service quality on purchase decisions and assesses the mediating function of consumer satisfaction among Generation Z consumers residing in Serang City. Methods: An explanatory quantitative survey involving 100 respondents chosen via purposive sampling was carried out. The data were gathered through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 20, encompassing validity and reliability examinations, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, coefficients of determination, and Sobel mediation analysis. Results: Both consumer trust and service quality exerted positive and significant direct effects on purchase decisions as well as on consumer satisfaction, whereas consumer satisfaction likewise positively and significantly influenced purchase decisions. The Sobel analyses verified significant mediation for trust (Z = 5.396) and for service quality (Z = 5.771). Within the simultaneous model, consumer satisfaction stayed significant, and the model accounted for 61.0% of the variance in purchase decisions. Conclusion: Consumer satisfaction occupies a pivotal mediating position in converting consumer trust and perceived service quality into streetwear purchase decisions on Shopee. These results suggest that sellers and marketplace managers ought to combine trust-building, service enhancement, and satisfaction management to reinforce purchasing outcomes.

latest.title: PRICING STRATEGY OPTIMIZATION FOR TRADITIONAL SCENTED CANDLE PRODUCTS IN DIFFERENTIATED LUXURY GOODS MARKETS
latest.abstract: Pricing strategy was a factor of competitive advantage in the markets for luxury goods in which product value, brand and differentiation are determinants of consumer’s choices. The approach may allow premium positioning and competitive advantage. This research investigates Pricing Strategy Optimization (PSO) for traditional scented candles, focusing on Consumer Price Perception (CPP), Brand Equity (BE), Sales Volume (SV), Customer Retention (CR), and Overall Market Performance (OMP). The research was carried out with 285 respondents from various fields including marketing managers, executives, and managers working in luxury candle companies. 5-point Likert scale structured questionnaires were distributed through online and physical mediums. Quantitative data were analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) 27 through descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and reliability analysis. It examined production costs, scent complexity, packaging exclusivity, and brand positioning as key pricing determinants. Results revealed positive correlations between pricing strategy optimization and overall market performance (r = 0.66), consumer price perception (r = 0.62), and brand equity (r = 0.58). Regression analysis indicated positive relationships with consumer price perception (β = 0.68), overall market performance (β = 0.65), brand equity (β = 0.62), customer retention (β = 0.59), and sales volume (β = 0.54). Reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable internal consistency across all variables. The results highlight the importance of including product differentiation, perceived value, and brand positioning into pricing decisions. latest.title: Research on the Mechanism of Offline Retail Visual Marketing Influence on Consumer Purchase Decisions
latest.venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
latest.abstract: With the the rapid growth of online shopping, offline physical stores face declining customer traffic and intensified competition. Compared with online consumption, which is largely based on information presented through digital interfaces, offline stores use visual elements such as display windows, lighting, product displays, and digital displays to influence consumers' perceptions of the store environment, product value, and brand image, affecting purchase decisions. Based on SOR (Stimulus-Body-Response) theory and referencing foreign research on retail and consumer behavior from 2023 to 2026, this paper analyzes the pathways of visual marketing's influence on consumer decision-making from three perspectives: visual perception, emotional experience, and consumer behavior. It further explores the moderating roles of individual consumer characteristics, shopping contexts, and product attributes in shaping the effects of visual marketing. The study finds that a coordinated and orderly visual environment can boost consumers' perceived value of stores and products, enhance positive emotions, extend dwell time, and promote purchase intention formation. Issues such as visual information overload and chaotic spatial layout increase consumers' psychological burden, hence reducing shopping experience and purchase tendencies. Based on the research results, this paper proposes optimization strategies for visual marketing practices, focusing on visual information hierarchy, spatial layout, product display, and scene matching.

latest.title: Sprinkle, Smell, Remember: How Sensory Salience and Ritualistic Use of Domino's Oregano Drive Nostalgia-Mediated Repurchase Intention and Brand Recall
latest.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
latest.abstract: Sensory cues serve as potent drivers of consumer behavior, yet their influence on nostalgia-mediated brand outcomes remains underexplored in the context of food service branding. This study investigates how sensory salience and ritualistic usage behaviors associated with Domino's oregano sachets influence repurchase intention and brand recall through three mediating mechanisms: nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, we collected data from 350 urban consumers with recent Domino's purchasing experience. Structural equation modeling via partial least squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test a comprehensive sensory-emotional branding framework. Results reveal that sensory salience, frequency of exposure, perceived uniqueness, and ritualistic usage behavior significantly predict mediating variables (nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort), which subsequently enhance repurchase intention and brand recall. Notably, sensory pleasure emerged as the strongest direct predictor of both outcome variables (β = 0.283 for brand recall, β = 0.280 for repurchase intention, p < 0.001). The model explains 87.6% of variance in brand recall and 88.9% in repurchase intention, demonstrating the explanatory power of the sensory-emotional framework. This research extends sensory branding literature by conceptualizing micro branding cues as ritualistic touchpoints and contributes practical insights for leveraging sensory marketing in highly competitive food service environments.

latest.title: Human-Centric Consumption Intelligence and Explainable AI (HCCI-XAI): Framework for Aspirational Consumption and Responsible Consumer Behaviour in Industry 5.0
latest.abstract: The connection between purchase behaviour, social identity, financial decision making and psychosocial well-being in the lives of young adults has changed due to the digitally mediated consumption. Young buyers consider several factors in the product evaluation process which include: words of the influencers, Brand image, Social media trends, product impressions, Social bandwagon effect and peer feedback as well. These are the advancements driven by automation and have been supported by Artificial Intelligence and advanced ML techniques to motivate consumers to make informed purchase decisions. From the consumers' perspectives these are all opportunities leading to “Self-expression” however raising questions related to financial pressure, consumer autonomy and the over interference of digital technologies in consumer’s purchase decision. In the new paradigm of Industry 5.0 consumers and machines interacted and coordinated with each other to facilitate the purchase process. However in the upcoming evolution of industry 6.0 three core elements: Human centric, Sustainability and Resilience shape up the entire digital ecosystem. Thus this study aims to create a Human-Centric Consumption Intelligence framework with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (HCCI-XAI) to explore the behavioural determinants of aspirational purchasing among the post-graduates students of Bengaluru city, India. The research was based on structured primary data collected in the period of March-July 2026 with the participation of 386 survey respondents and 35 recorded variables. The six behavioural constructs studied in this article include: Masstige Perception, Symbolic Consumption Orientation, Value Consciousness, Consumer Orientation, Digital Influence and Ethical Orientation. latest.title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
latest.abstract: Abstract Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when facing ambiguous cues in mate-choice decisions, yet how such advice optimizes outcomes remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Computational modeling quantified the decision optimization parameter ( β ). It showed that only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) model—best fit behavioral data, indicating that optimization arises from reciprocal adaptation rather than one-way influence. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more effectively promoted optimization. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that trial-level INS predicted momentary optimization, while task-level INS robustly forecasted overall decision improvement. Together, these findings demonstrate that decision optimization emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice enhances decision quality and social well-being.

latest.title: When does transparency matter for consumers’ circular decisions? Visibility and traceability in closed-loop supply chains
latest.abstract: Markets are increasingly demanding greater supply chain transparency, yet this remains a significant challenge for many companies. Understanding whether and what type of information to disclose represents a significant challenge for companies, particularly when the information pertains to circular initiatives, such as those involved in closed-loop activities. This study, grounded in signaling theory, explores the effect of disclosing closed-loop supply chain information on consumers' intentions. We selected consumers as our unit of analysis for the active role they can play when referring to companies’ closed-loop initiatives, such as purchasing recycled products or participating in take-back programs. To test the hypotheses, two scenario-based experiments are conducted. The primary aim of the studies is to operationalize supply chain transparency through its visibility and traceability components in a closed-loop supply chain context. A second objective is to examine the effectiveness of transparency in closed-loop supply chains, analyzing how the two components influence consumer outcomes across different phases of the customer journey. The findings contribute to the growing literature on supply chain transparency, identifying the boundaries of signaling theory and offering insights for managers on strategic investments in transparency.

latest.title: Uncovering the unseen: a multi-scalar scoping review of short-term rentals and urban transformation
latest.abstract: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building on PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it systematically maps 161 studies published between 2009 and 2025, identifying key patterns in the economic, environmental, spatial, and regulatory analysis of STRs. The findings reveal that while STRs foster tourism growth and local development, they also exacerbate housing unaffordability, gentrification, and overtourism. The literature remains dominated by data-driven methods, spatial analysis, econometric modelling, and machine learning yet exhibits strong geographic biases and limited integration across disciplines. Results highlight the growing professionalisation of hosts, the role of digital technologies in reshaping governance, and the urgent need for adaptive, sustainability-oriented regulation. By consolidating fragmented debates, this review offers a multidimensional synthesis that informs smart city planning, digital governance, and the pursuit of the Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary tourism destinations.

latest.abstract: This research aimed to study: 1) consumers’ personal characteristics; 2) consumer acceptance; 3) the level of importance of marketing mix factors; and 4) the factors influencing consumer acceptance of hybrid chicken steak with black pepper sauce in Phatthalung province. Data were collected from 400 respondents using questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations) and stepwise multiple regression analysis. The results were as follow: 1) The findings revealed that most consumers were female, aged 21–40 years, held a bachelor’s degree, were single, and worked in government agencies or state enterprises. 2) Consumers accepted it due to its appetizing aroma, pleasant taste, and deliciousness. Most preferred a price range of 50–100 Baht and a package weight of 101–200 grams, and showed an intention to continue purchasing the product in the future. 3) The overall marketing mix factors were rated at the highest level (\bar{x}=4.56), with product factors receiving the highest importance, followed by distribution channels, sales promotion, and price. 4) Age had a statistically significant negative effect on product acceptance at the 0.05 level, while product and distribution channel factors were the key determinants influencing consumer acceptance. These findings highlight consumers’ emphasis on product quality and accessibility. They may serve as guidelines for developing processed livestock products, adding value to agricultural products, and improving marketing strategies for community products in Phatthalung province.

latest.title: Analysis of Students’ Considerations in Selecting Products Based on Needs and Financial Capacity
latest.venue: Journal of Management Entrepreneurship and Tourism
latest.abstract: This study examined how university students evaluated products before purchasing, the factors shaping their choices, their approaches to purchasing within financial constraints, and the prioritization of needs over wants. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, drawing on interviews with five students at Universitas Islam Negeri Prof. K.H. Saifuddin Zuhri Purwokerto. Interview data were analyzed through reduction, thematic presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings showed that students considered price, product quality, usefulness, durability, and the compatibility of purchases with their needs. Across respondents, price and quality were frequently considered, whereas the importance attached to promotions varied. Discounts, promotions, and trends also influenced choices, although they did not consistently outweigh practical considerations. Students managed limited allowances by allocating budgets, recording expenses, postponing purchases, saving, or seeking more affordable alternatives. When funds were insufficient, postponement was a commonly reported response. Daily living and academic requirements generally took precedence over discretionary purchases. Some respondents nevertheless reported difficulty managing money or balancing price against quality. The findings offer a context-specific account of purchasing considerations rather than evidence of causal effects or patterns representative of students elsewhere. The study concluded that students’ purchasing decisions reflected ongoing negotiations between product value, perceived necessity, and available financial resources.

latest.title: Impact of AI Generated Content and Perceived Personalization on Purchase Intention with Mediating Input of Brand Credibility in FMCG Industry in Pakistan
latest.venue: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
latest.abstract: This research study investigated the empirical impact of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase intention with mediating input of brand credibility in case of FMCG sector in Pakistan. It investigated both direct and indirect of AI generated content and perceived personalization on purchase along with the impact of AI generated content on perceived personalization in Pakistan. The study used quantitative research approach and employed deductive approach to build hypotheses. Those were tested with application of statistical techniques i.e. structural equation model using PLS-Smart as software. The study targeted the FMCG sector in Pakistan and used convenience sampling technique to extract with the required number of responses i.e. 384 using questionnaire as data collection tool. The study followed with the survey based method to collect with the required number of response in the limited period of time. The study revealed that there is significant impact of AI Generated Content on Brand Credibility, Perceived Personalization and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4294, 0.5758 and 0.5211having significance value of 0.0000, 0.000 and 0.000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Perceived Personalization on Brand Credibility and Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4857 and 0.3093 having significance value of 0.0000 and 0.0000 respectively. There is also a significant impact of Brand Credibility on Purchase Intention with coefficient value of 0.4574 having significance value of 0.0000. FMCG companies should develop accurate, engaging, and personalized AI-generated content to enhance brand credibility and consumer confidence. latest.title: An Analysis of the Factors Influencing Consumer Behavior in the Purchase of Food Products
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Management and Accounting
latest.abstract: Food purchasing behavior reflects interactions among consumer characteristics, psychological evaluations, marketing stimuli, and purchasing circumstances. This study aimed to identify, classify, and synthesize factors influencing consumer behavior in purchasing food products. A descriptive qualitative literature review was conducted using secondary data from journal articles, academic books, and previous research reports. The original review covered literature published between 1991 and 2023, with findings analyzed through thematic synthesis and comparative interpretation. Six determinant categories were identified: cultural, social, personal, psychological, marketing-mix, and situational factors. Comparative evidence revealed differences in the dominant factors across food categories and purchasing environments. Price was dominant in instant noodle purchasing, with a reported influence of 12.15%, while psychological factors were most influential in steamed layer cake purchasing. Product attributes were most decisive in a selected food outlet, whereas purchasing time was the strongest factor in a fast-food restaurant setting. These differences indicated that purchasing behavior depended on product characteristics, consumer evaluations, and transaction circumstances rather than a universally dominant determinant. The study contributes an integrated conceptual framework for interpreting heterogeneous purchasing influences and supports context-sensitive marketing strategies. Differences in research designs and measurements limit direct statistical comparisons and causal generalization.

latest.title: Artificially influential: examining the impact of virtual influencers on non-followers’ behavior
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the limited understanding of how unfamiliar non-followers respond to virtual versus human influencers encountered through algorithmically curated feeds. This study tests whether disclosure that a seemingly human influencer is AI-generated lowers perceived authenticity, producing negative expectation disconfirmation that reduces engagement and purchase intentions. Design/methodology/approach Two between-subjects online experiments with US non-followers (n = 303 and n = 316) were conducted through CloudResearch Connect. Measurement validity was assessed using confirmatory factor analysis in SmartPLS 4, and hypotheses were tested using PROCESS serial mediation analyses with bootstrapping. Findings Across both studies, virtual influencer disclosure significantly lowered perceived authenticity, which generated more negative expectation disconfirmation and reduced engagement intentions. In Study 2, this serial process extended to lower purchase intentions. The hypothesized serial indirect effects were significant. Practical implications Brands using human-presenting virtual influencers with unfamiliar audiences should treat disclosure as expectation management by clearly identifying the influencer as AI-generated or virtual from initial exposure. Managers should also recognize that disclosure may lower perceived authenticity, engagement and purchase intentions. Originality/value This study examines an underexplored stage of virtual influencer exposure involving unfamiliar non-followers. latest.title: The interaction effect of emotional message appeals and emotions on travel intention
latest.abstract: Purpose Although message appeal is often used in destination marketing, the effectiveness of positive and negative message appeals remains unknown. Two online experiments were conducted to answer this research question. Based on the emotion-congruent effect, this study proves that when a customer is in a negative emotional state, advertisements with a negative message appeal increase visit intention, whereas when a customer is in a positive emotional state, advertisements with a positive message appeal increase visit intention. This study aims to identify empathy as the mediator explaining the mechanism underlying the interaction effects. This study not only contributes to destination marketing research by identifying customers’ emotions as a moderating variable in examining the effectiveness of destination advertising message appeals, but also offers practical implications for destination marketers, enabling them to segment their advertising strategies based on customers’ emotions.

latest.title: Cognitive Offloading to Generative AI: A Theoretical Framework for Memory, Metacognition, and Consumer Decision-Making
latest.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) increasingly mediates product search, evaluation, and choice, consumer cognition is becoming distributed across human–AI systems. This shift challenges a largely unexamined assumption in advertising theory: that persuasion operates through cognitive elaboration within the individual consumer. Drawing on cognitive offloading research from cognitive psychology, we develop the CogOffload framework to explain when consumers delegate cognitive work to Gen-AI and what consequences follow. A seven-stage delegation continuum maps increasing levels of offloading, and a value-based cost-benefit framework identifies its antecedents and the moderators that shape how consumers weigh them. We propose three clusters of outcomes. First, offloading weakens memory for brands and product attributes while strengthening memory for AI-generated summaries. Second, it inflates metacognitive self-esteem and decision confidence, producing AI-induced overconfidence that reduces further information-seeking. Third, effects on decision quality depend on AI reliability: when AI is unreliable, verifying AI recommendations imposes cognitive and emotional costs but can restore impaired memory and recalibrate inflated confidence. Seven propositions and three long-term conjectures extend these effects to consumer autonomy, competence erosion, and brand loyalty. Together, the CogOffload framework positions advertising in the era of Gen-AI as operating within a distributed system of human and artificial cognition.

latest.title: Dynamic mechanism of digital technology empowering green innovation in manufacturing enterprises
latest.abstract: Although the dual digital and green transformation has become a strategic imperative for manufacturing firms, whether and how digital technology effectively drives green innovation remains contested. This debate largely stems from concerns regarding digital divides and the potential for diminishing returns caused by excessive investment. To address this theoretical gap, this study develops a differential game model to examine the dynamic mechanisms through which digital technology enables green innovation across three distinct stages of the product lifecycle: research and development focused on green knowledge accumulation, manufacturing focused on product greenness, and post-sale operations focused on green service. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate three primary findings. First, digital technology, knowledge accumulation, product greenness, and service quality all exert positive effects on overall green innovation performance, with the marginal effects being stronger in the initial period. Second, green knowledge accumulation plays a dominant role relative to product greenness and green service. Third, the relationship between digital input and green innovation benefits follows an inverted U-shaped trajectory, which is regulated by a critical threshold determined by the ratio of technology sensitivity to application costs. These findings offer theoretical explanations for the digital divide phenomenon in green innovation and provide practical guidance for manufacturing firms seeking to optimize their digital investments and avoid overinvestment traps during sustainability transitions.

latest.title: Frontal alpha asymmetry and instructed satisfaction-rating changes after price presentation: An exploratory pilot study
latest.abstract: This exploratory pilot study asked whether frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) recorded while a price is displayed varies with the satisfaction-rating change a consumer then makes. Twenty-one participants completed two blocks of 30 trials: view a product, give a pre-price rating (1-9), see the price, give a post-price rating, which they were instructed to change except at the scale limits. The change is described by its direction and magnitude (|Δ|, provisionally labeled Decision Momentum), two descriptions of one difference score. FAA was computed from relative alpha power at F3/F4 over 0-3 s after price onset on average-referenced data. Inference rests on 19 participants and 820 trials. The primary pooled test of the direction × magnitude interaction was inconclusive (β=-0.051, 95% CI [-0.111,0.009], p = 0.093). An exploratory block-stratified analysis found an interaction in the first block (β=-0.087, 95% CI [-0.152,-0.021], p = 0.010), although neither of its two component slopes differed clearly from zero. Support varied across specifications, and five alternative operationalizations of FAA did not reproduce it. The same model applied to the window before price onset, where the predictors cannot yet reflect the price, produced an interaction of comparable or larger size pooled and in the second block. In the first block, the direct comparison did not establish a difference between windows, and adjusting for pre-price FAA left the first-block estimate unchanged (p = 0.008); in the second block, the two windows did differ (p = 0.021), the association being present before the price and not after it. latest.title: Moderating Effect of Self-Brand Congruity on Purchase Intention of Luxury Brands
latest.abstract: This study examines moderating effect of self-brand congruity on purchase intention of luxury brands. A cumulative approach to analyze purchase intention of luxury brands is presented by combining the behavioral aspects of consumers and personality of the brand. The driving forces that lead to a brand purchase are very important. The question arises that what are the drivers of the luxury brand purchase intention considering the fact that in many cases the same benefits can be acquired from an ordinary brand. Certainly, the functional benefits are the same but there might be some drivers or attitudes that derive luxury brands purchase. This paper identifies those factors (self-expression attitude and self-presentation attitude) and empirically investigates their relationship with consumer’s purchase intention of luxury brands. This study also examines mediating role of affective attitude in relationship between social function attitudes and purchase intentions towards luxury brands. Data is collected from 400 customers living in Lahore and Gujranwala cities, Pakistan. Multiple regression is employed to test relationship between social function attitudes and purchase intention. Bootstrapping method has been used to check the mediation and moderation. Findings show that social function attitude (self-expression & self-presentation attitude) positively influence the purchase intentions towards luxury brand. Moreover, findings confirm mediating role of affective attitude and moderating role of self-brand congruity. This shows that brand personality is very important factor in brand positioning specially for luxury brands where symbolic benefits are far more important than functional benefits.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
