latest.title: The dark side of GenAI in the workplace: technostress, loneliness, and the buffering role of transformational leadership
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming the workplace, but it also introduces technostress that affects employees’ psychological states and behavioral consequences. However, existing research has yet to offer an integrated framework that explicates the socio-emotional processes and work outcomes of GenAI integration, along with the boundary conditions that moderate these relationships. To bridge this gap, this study integrates the Stressor-Strain-Outcome (SSO) framework and the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory to examine how GenAI-induced technostress influences work loneliness and work effort. Using survey data from 290 public school teachers in Taiwan, this study finds that GenAI-induced technostress is negatively associated with work effort indirectly through work loneliness, whereas its direct effect is not statistically significant. Moreover, transformational leadership weakens the negative relationship between work loneliness and work effort; however, it does not significantly moderate the GenAI-induced technostress-work loneliness link nor the overall moderated mediation effect. This study contributes to the literature by proposing a technostress-work loneliness-work effort pathway from a resource depletion perspective, and by elucidating the boundary conditions under which transformational leadership, as a critical resource buffer, functions in this mechanism in the context of GenAI-driven work environments. From a practical standpoint, these findings offer actionable insights for organizations seeking to foster sustainable GenAI integration while safeguarding employee well-being.

latest.title: Entrepreneurship, Start-ups, MSME, Innovation, Ecosystem and New- Age Business Models; Emerging Trends and Opportunities In India
latest.abstract: Entrepreneurship, start-ups and micro, small and Medium Enterprise (MSMEs) have emerged as important components of economic development, employment generation and innovation. The rapid development of digital technologies, artificial intelligence, fintech, e-commerce, social media platforms and cloud-based service has significantly transformed the manner in which businesses are created, operated and scaled. At the same time, the emergence of new-age business models such as platform businesses, subscription models, direct to consumer models, sharing-economy models, digital marketplaces and technology enabled service models has created new opportunities for entrepreneur and MSME. This paper examine the interrelationship between entrepreneurship, startups, MSME, innovation ecosystem and new-age business models in the contemporary Indian business environment. The study adopt a conceptual and descriptive research approach based on secondary source, including academic literature, Government report and institutional publication. The paper identifies major factors influencing entrepreneurial capabilities, incubation, mentoring, market access, networking and government support.

latest.title: Exploring intangible cultural heritage in contemporary Pennsylvania Dutch food culture through food memories
latest.abstract: Introduction Food memories provide an important yet underexamined means through which communities articulate, transmit, and negotiate intangible cultural heritage, particularly when commercial heritagization privileges selected foods and cultural representations. This study examines how contemporary Pennsylvania Dutch cultural insiders construct food memories and what those narratives reveal about the maintenance and transmission of Pennsylvania Dutch food culture. Methods Using a narrative-based approach, we analyzed semi-structured interviews with seven cultural insiders, including chefs, home cooks, food-business owners, and cookbook authors, from Berks and York counties in Pennsylvania. We analyzed our interviewees’ narratives using a hybrid deductive–inductive approach guided by an adapted framework for analyzing food memories across four dimensions: embodied knowledge, emotions, people and communality, and evocative settings. Results Our participants’ narratives suggested that food-related knowledge is passed on through experience, family connections, and regional and seasonal food practices. Their food memories also suggested that assimilation, commodification, and heritagization processes can marginalize certain food practices and meanings important to community members. Discussion We contend that food memories may be understood as examples of narratively constructed intangible heritage through which culturally meaningful knowledge, skills, values, and practices become visible. Empirically, this article contributes to the study of food memories by providing insider perspectives concerning an underexamined regional food culture and by adapting a food memory framework for use in narrative interviewing.

latest.title: Promoting responsible tourism using generative AI nudges
latest.abstract: Purpose With rapid modernization and globalization, responsible tourism practices at cultural heritage sites are in decline, as many visitors disengage from activities like volunteering, donating or mindful visits. This shift presents a significant challenge for governments, organizations and societies working to promote meaningful interactions with cultural heritage. Encouraging responsible tourism – where visitors respect local cultures while minimizing negative impacts – is crucial. generative artificial intelligence (GAI) offers an emerging avenue for innovative management practices, providing personalized and emotionally resonant digital nudges that can influence visitor engagement. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding which types of nudges are most effective across cultural contexts. This study aims to investigate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven nudges delivered on emotional response and engagement, aiming to foster responsible tourism behaviour. Design/methodology/approach Using a mixed-methods approach, this study adopted a three-stage investigation. Firstly, this study conducted a content analysis gathered from 262 articles via web scrapping which identified five key themes surrounding responsible tourism. Stage two consisted of 25 in-depth interviews, which provided deeper insights on the factors influencing emotional response towards cultural heritage tourism. In stage 3, this study conducted 300 experiments and surveys, focusing on responses to six cultural nudge images representing Indian and UK cultures. Each image was categorized into neutral, positive and negative nudges, capturing participants’ engagement. Findings The findings suggest that AI-driven nudges significantly enhance tourists’ emotional responses (β = 0.108,

latest.title: A 2-layered game-theoretic deep learning model for predicting lodging demand: SHAP and nash equilibrium
latest.venue: Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management
latest.abstract: Abstract Forecasting tourism demand is critical for pricing and revenue management, yet most advanced machine learning models operate as “black boxes,” limiting interpretability and trust. This study introduces an explainable, game-theoretic hybrid deep learning framework for predicting short-term rental demand. This study incorporates game theory in two layers: a cooperative game and a competitive game. Using 729,888 daily observations from 1,852 Airbnb listings in Ann Arbor, Michigan, we compare traditional models (regression, SARIMAX) with advanced architectures (FCNN, LSTM, Transformer, and a Transformer–LSTM hybrid). Game theory is used in two layers: cooperative game (SHAP) and competitive game (classic Nash equilibrium). SHAP creates an explainable deep learning model to quantify each feature’s contribution. The best-performing model (FCNN) was further used to simulate a 3x3 pricing game between pairs within 4 submarkets. Results show that deep learning models significantly outperform traditional baselines, while SHAP-based feature attribution and clustering enhance transparency and strategic insight. The competitive games shed light on the characteristics and dynamics of each submarket. This research offers insights to revenue managers, policymakers, and operators.

latest.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN REDUCING MARKETING COSTS AND ENHANCING PROFITABILITY: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY ON START-UPS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
latest.abstract: This study investigates the empirical relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in marketing functions and dual outcomes of marketing cost reduction and profitability enhancement among start-ups in developing economies. A cross-national, quantitative survey-based design was employed across five countries—Nigeria, Egypt, Kenya, Vietnam, and Bangladesh—yielding 412 valid responses from founders and C-suite executives. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics 29, SmartPLS 4.0 (Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling [PLS-SEM]), and R 4.3.2 (lavaan package for confirmatory factor analysis [CFA]). AI adoption in marketing was found to reduce overall marketing expenditure by a mean of 31.4% and increase gross profit margin (GPM) by 18.9 percentage points relative to non-adopting cohorts. Predictive analytics (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) and programmatic advertising (β = 0.38, p < 0.001) exhibited the strongest direct effects on cost reduction, while AI-augmented customer relationship management (CRM) demonstrated the highest impact on customer lifetime value (CLV) (β = 0.45, p < 0.001). Multi-group analysis (MGA) revealed significant moderation by national AI readiness index (NAIRI) (χ² difference = 34.7, df = 10, p = 0.0002), making this one of the first large-scale cross-national empirical studies to simultaneously quantify AI-driven marketing cost savings and profitability gains across five developing-country start-up ecosystems.

latest.title: Technostress and telemedicine in rural communities: insights from healthcare professionals in the Italian Dolomites
latest.abstract: Introduction: In Italy, many facilities have started adopting telemedicine services since their regulation in 2020.Rural areas mainly benefit from telemedicine implementation due to their geographic features.We investigated the interests, attitudes, and perceptions of healthcare providers operating in the Italian Dolomites regarding the adoption of telemedicine.Furthermore, we explored the relationship between technostress and the intention to integrate telemedicine services during daily practices.Methods: We developed a structured interview protocol based on existing literature and following the key principles of constructivist grounded theory to investigate five areas of interest in telemedicine.After the interview, participants completed the Italian version of the Technostress Creators Scale (TCS) to evaluate the current technostress experienced in work activities, and a TCS-adapted version to measure technostress values generated through telemedicine services.Results: A content analysis of the interviews highlighted four main factors that can help communities more readily accept telemedicine services: the convenience of not having to travel, the ageing population, cost savings, and a sense of community.Regarding the scales, there were positive significant correlations between most of the subscales.Discussion: Our findings confirm that telemedicine fosters perceived security and service quality in rural settings.Despite moderate technostress, professionals remain supportive, highlighting the role of perceived usefulness.Key barriers include low digital literacy and reduced social contact, underscoring the need for strong patient-provider relationships and targeted digital r

latest.title: Mapping the Attitudinal Continuum Toward AI in Tourism: An Explainable Segmentation of a Croatian Consumer Sample
latest.abstract: This study examines Croatian consumers’ perceptions and attitudes towards artificial intelligence (AI) applications in tourism and hospitality services through advanced machine learning clustering analysis. Using K-means clustering with shapley additive explanations feature importance analysis on a non-probability online sample of 592 respondents, the analysis found that AI attitudes in this sample form a continuum rather than densely separated groups and partitions that continuum into four interpretable profiles. Emotional response to anticipated AI interaction and age were among the features most important for distinguishing cluster membership in a Random Forest classification model trained to distinguish the four segments, alongside income and education; because these were clustering inputs, and segments formed on attitudes alone do not differ in them, their prominence reflects how the partition was constructed rather than a link between socioeconomic position and AI attitudes. A supplementary validation analysis indicated that segment membership reflects attitudinal variation rather than independently predicting prior AI-related behaviour. The partition yielded four profiles: AI Enthusiasts (21.1%), AI Sceptics (19.9%), Pragmatic Users (33.3%), and Cautious Adopters (25.7%). Convergent evidence from K-means, DBSCAN, Gaussian mixture, and Gower/PAM clustering indicates that the enthusiastic-to-resistant gradient is robust across methods, whereas the placement of individual respondents along it is metric-dependent. The profiles are therefore presented as an instrumental description of attitudinal variation rather than as discrete consumer types and are informative for communication strategy at the aggregate level rather than for individual-level targeting. As the stud

latest.title: Digital marketing analytics capabilities and firm performance: Cross-cultural evidence from emerging markets
latest.abstract: Digital marketing analytics capabilities (DMACs) are widely promoted as a performance driver in emerging markets, yet whether their returns are universal or context-dependent remains unclear. Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), dynamic capabilities theory, and institutional theory, this study tests a sequential mediation model in which DMACs shape firm performance through market orientation and market responsiveness, with institutional context (digital infrastructure, governance quality, talent availability, and market maturity) moderating this pathway. Using structural equation modeling (SEM) on survey and financial data from 641 firms across Ghana, India, China, and Mexico, the model achieved acceptable fit and explained 58 percent of the variance in firm performance (R² = 0.58). Market orientation and market responsiveness sequentially mediated the DMAC–performance relationship, accounting for 42 percent of total effects. Institutional context significantly moderated the direct effect, which ranged from β = 0.15 in low-institutional-quality contexts to β = 0.41 in high-institutional-quality contexts—a 2.7-fold difference. These findings indicate that identical analytics investments yield systematically different returns depending on institutional readiness, challenging assumptions of universal capability effectiveness and offering emerging-market firms and policymakers a more conditional basis for analytics strategy.

latest.title: Exploring the user experience and improvement strategies of AI chatbots on China’s Meituan instant retail platform from the perspective of generation Z users
latest.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is profoundly transforming traditional service models. In recent years, AI chatbots have gradually become a common smart service on instant retail platforms. However, existing research still lacks sufficient understanding of users’ actual experiences when using this type of AI service primarily based on intelligent interaction. This study focuses on the AI chatbots on Meituan’s instant retail platform, examines the experiences and conditions of Generation Z when using AI chatbots, and proposes strategies and recommendations for improving the user experience. The study examined the research questions by combining user interviews, the KANO model, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process. The main findings are as follows: Generation Z has the highest demand for the intelligent interaction experience provided by AI chatbots. At the same time, the degree of importance of needs such as personalized AI chatbot avatar, humanized AI interaction, AI personalized recommendations, and intelligent emotional perception interaction is relatively high. This indicates that Generation Z’s demands for AI chatbots have already expanded from simple needs such as consulting about products and orders to diversified online personalized consumption experiences. For example, inquiring about the usage rules of platform coupons, receiving intelligent recommendations based on personal dietary habits, and other diversified online lifestyles. Based on this, this study proposes experience enhancement strategies for optimizing the dialogue mechanism between users and AI chatbots, improving the anthropomorphic level of the interface dialogue mechanism, providing visualized presentation of intelligent service progress, and providing functional settings for user privacy protecti

latest.title: An integrative model of career adaptability, innovative behavior, and work skills on public sector performance: The mediating role of career development in local government
latest.abstract: Purpose: As digital disruption and bureaucratic reform continue to reshape the public sector, strategic transformation is required to enhance service effectiveness. This study investigates how institutional career development systems channel part of individuals' capabilities into sustained performance, while another part remains unconverted. The study further develops and tests a human resource development model linking career adaptability, innovative work behaviour, and work skills with employee performance, with career development serving as a mediating mechanism.Design/methodology/approach: Survey data from 372 civil servants across 34 Regional Government Organisations (Organisasi Perangkat Daerah, OPD) in Lahat Regency, South Sumatra, Indonesia, were analysed with variance-based structural equation modelling in SmartPLS 4.0, using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples.Findings: The results indicate that career adaptability (β = 0.131; p = 0.036), innovative work behaviour (β = 0.175; p = 0.047), and work skills (β = 0.131; p = 0.023) each exert a significant positive effect on employee performance. Career development mediates the relationships between career adaptability and work skills with performance, whereas the mediating pathway for innovative work behaviour did not reach conventional significance (β = 0.146; p = 0.056), even though innovative work behaviour produced the strongest path towards career development (β = 0.503; p < 0.001).Research limitations/implications: Theoretically, the contribution of this study lies not in the combination of constructs, but in advancing the concept of capability codification the extent to which an individual capability is formally categorised within promotion criteria as a boundary condition that may explain the observed inconsistency

latest.title: Perceived content attractiveness and travel intention in countryside tourism short videos: comparing emotional arousal and need for escapism
latest.venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
latest.abstract: Introduction Countryside-themed tourism short videos have become important sources of destination information and travel inspiration, yet the affective and motivational responses associated with attractive content may not be equally relevant to travel intention. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, this study examined the associations among perceived content attractiveness, emotional arousal, need for escapism, and travel intention and directly compared the two specific indirect associations. Methods Perceived content attractiveness was conceptualized as a higher-order appraisal comprising destination attractiveness, presenter attractiveness, and video design attractiveness. Data were collected through an online survey of a convenience sample of 434 Chinese social media users who had previously viewed short videos about countryside life or rural tourism. Structural equation modeling and bias-corrected bootstrapping were used to examine the proposed relationships. Results Perceived content attractiveness was positively associated with travel intention, emotional arousal, and need for escapism. Need for escapism was positively associated with travel intention, whereas the unique structural association between emotional arousal and travel intention was not significant. The specific indirect association through need for escapism was significant, whereas that through emotional arousal was not. A bootstrap comparison further showed that the specific indirect association through need for escapism was significantly larger than that through emotional arousal. Discussion These findings distinguish experiential activation from restoration-oriented motivational relevance and suggest that need for escapism is more closely associated with travel intention than emotion

latest.title: Digital Economy, Technological Innovation, and Entrepreneurial Activity: Evidence from Chinese Provinces
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital economy development and enterprise upgrading in China, with particular attention to the mediating roles of green technology innovation and entrepreneurial activity. It also investigates provincial heterogeneity and conducts robustness tests. The analysis uses panel data for 30 Chinese provinces covering 2010–2024, obtained from the National Bureau of Statistics of China. Fixed-effects regression models are employed to examine the relationship between digital economy development and enterprise upgrading. The results indicate a significant positive association between digital economy development and enterprise upgrading, with a coefficient of 0.52 in the full model. Green technology innovation and entrepreneurial activity are identified as important mediating mechanisms through which the digital economy may contribute to enterprise upgrading. The provincial heterogeneity analysis indicates that the digital economy is positively associated with enterprise upgrading across the regions examined, although the magnitude of the association varies; the estimated effect is more pronounced in the eastern and midwestern regions. The findings remain robust across the reported robustness tests. The results further suggest that the digital economy can facilitate innovation by enabling rapid prototyping, data-driven decision-making, and more efficient resource allocation, while reducing operating and market-entry costs for entrepreneurs. The study recommends strengthening digital literacy programmes, improving cybersecurity, and developing regionally responsive digital economy policies to promote more balanced development across eastern, central, and western China.

latest.title: The Instagram paradox: a mediation analysis of consumer orientations, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions & Instagram motivations shaping purchase intention of sustainable apparel in India
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines how distinctive consumer orientations - Thrifty, Frugal, Moral, and Shopper influence sustainable apparel purchase intention among Indian Instagram users. Grounded in Uses and Gratifications theory and the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study examines the parallel mediating roles played by inherent psychological, cognitive and deep structures and external stimuli of Instagram motivation in rendering consumer orientation to purchase intention, thus presenting an empirical justification for the ‘Instagram Paradox’ in the framework of sustainable fashion. Methods A quantitative survey was administered to 285 Instagram users and followers of sustainable apparel brands in India, recruited via snowball sampling. Factor Analyses was conducted to validate constructs spanning consumer orientation, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions, Instagram motivations, and purchase intention. Results K-means cluster analysis identified four distinct consumer orientation segments. Four parallel mediation models tested whether psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions along with Instagram motivation mediated the relationship between each consumer orientation and purchase intention. Discussion Across all the mediation models, psychological, cognitive and deep structure constructs emerged as the sole significant mediator, while Instagram motivation consistently failed to generate a significant indirect effect on purchase intention in any model, constituting the central empirical evidence for the Instagram Paradox.

latest.title: Digital Pedagogies for Entrepreneurship Education in South Africa: Opportunities and Limitations
latest.venue: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
latest.abstract: This research is situated in the field of entrepreneurship education in the South African higher education context. The analysis is conducted through a systematic literature review with qualitative thematic synthesis, grounded in constructivist and connectivist learning theory. Digital pedagogies provide clear opportunities for application in this field. These approaches may improve learning accessibility, flexibility and student engagement, and promote experiential and interactive learning based on constructivist principles by using tools such as learning management systems, simulations, and online collaboration platforms. Yet, the implementation of these pedagogies is still encountering numerous challenges: the persistent local digital divide, disparities in digital literacy between teachers and students, inadequate technological infrastructure, insufficient funding, and institutional barriers stemming from the lack of a comprehensive digital strategy have impeded their widespread adoption.Furthermore, while digital platforms support learning, they may not fully replicate the complexity of real-world entrepreneurial experiences, underscoring the importance of blended learning approaches. The central argument advanced in this paper is that digital technology alone cannot transform entrepreneurship education; its effectiveness depends on pedagogical integration, institutional capacity and the surrounding socio-economic context. Building on this argument, the study proposes a conceptual framework linking digital infrastructure and institutional readiness, digital capability, digital pedagogical practice and experiential entrepreneurial learning outcomes, and offers practical recommendations for improving teaching and learning practices in South African higher education.

latest.title: Strategic Decision-Making for Innovation in Emerging Organisations: An Adaptive Framework for VUCA Environments
latest.venue: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
latest.abstract: Strategic decision-making and innovation are critical to the competitiveness of emerging organisations operating in volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous (VUCA) environments. This paper examines how emerging organisations can make adaptive strategic decisions while pursuing innovation under conditions of environmental uncertainty. Using O’mari Zimbabwe, a corporate-backed financial technology (fintech) venture of Old Mutual Digital Services, the paper aims to develop an adaptive strategic decision-making framework for innovation in a VUCA environment. The study adopts a qualitative case-study and documentary research design, drawing on publicly available information on O’mari and Zimbabwe’s fintech environment. The analysis applies PESTEL, SWOT, Porter’s Five Forces, stakeholder analysis, and the VUCA framework. The theoretical foundation integrates the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities, organisational ambidexterity, contingency theory, effectuation, bounded rationality, institutional theory, and disruptive innovation. Findings indicate that O’mari’s innovation and competitive advantage depend not only on Old Mutual’s brand, resources, regulatory expertise and institutional legitimacy, but also on its capacity to reconfigure these resources, experiment responsibly, build ecosystem partnerships, strengthen customer trust and continuously learn from environmental change. The paper develops the Adaptive Inclusive Finance Decision Cycle (AIFDC), comprising seven interconnected stages: sensing, problem framing, resource-based option selection, controlled experimentation, trust and regulatory gating, modular scaling, and learning and resource reallocation. The paper concludes that strategic decision-making in emerging organisations under VUCA conditions should be

latest.title: Boas práticas em serviços de alimentação e ESG trilhas da produção científica e aproximações com o turismo
latest.venue: Revista Rosa dos Ventos - Turismo e Hospitalidade
latest.abstract: This study aimed to map the paths of scientific production that articulate good practices in food services and ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) axes, through bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review. The relationship with tourism was established by recognizing food services as activities integrated into the dynamics of destinations, the tourist experience, and sustainability. The findings indicate that, although there is scientific production on food services, there is still a scarcity of studies that relate, in an integrated way, good practices, food services, and ESG. Bibliometric analysis and the systematic review, which deepened the analysis based on the only open-access study with two of the three searched terms, highlighted the incipient nature of the field. It is identified that there is a relevant theoretical gap and possibilities for rapprochement between good practices, ESG, and food services, especially in tourism, due to the territorial, sociocultural, environmental, and managerial impacts of these enterprises on destinations.

latest.title: Impact of AI Chatbot Service Quality on Brand Loyalty Mediated by Customer Satisfaction in Generation Z Shopee Users in Medan
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has driven e-commerce platforms to adopt AI Chatbots to enhance customer service efficiency; however, the performance of this technology is frequently challenged by high user expectations. This study aims to empirically test and analyze the impact of AI Chatbot service quality on brand loyalty, and to prove the mediating role of customer satisfaction among Generation Z Shopee users in Medan City. This quantitative explanatory study collected primary data through an online structured Likert-scale questionnaire. The sample size is determined to be 385 respondents using the Lemeshow formula alongside a purposive sampling technique. Data analysis was conducted using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach with SmartPLS software. The structural testing (bootstrapping) results prove that AI Chatbot service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Customer satisfaction also has a positive and significant effect on brand loyalty. Directly, AI Chatbot service quality positively impacts brand loyalty. Furthermore, customer satisfaction is proven to significantly mediate the relationship between AI Chatbot service quality and brand loyalty. This study concludes that a responsive and accurate virtual agent does not merely function as an operational support tool but acts as an essential strategic asset that triggers user expectation confirmation, which ultimately transforms a short-term digital interaction experience into a long-term behavioral commitment.

latest.title: From Predictive Analytics to Supervised Agentic Decision Intelligence: Transforming Retail, CPG and Supply Chain Operations Through AI
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This research paper examines the evolution of enterprise analytics from traditional Business Intelligence and predictive modelling toward supervised agentic decision intelligence. The study focuses on Retail, Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Marketing Measurement and Supply Chain Management, exploring how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and specialized AI agents can improve enterprise decision-making. The paper presents Naukr.ai as an industry case study of a vertical AI platform focused on Retail and CPG analytics. It examines the company's four primary Agent Hubs: Supply Chain Agent Hub – Demand forecasting, inventory optimization, replenishment intelligence and store signals. Media Agent Hub – Agentic Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), media measurement and marketing budget optimization. Reporting Agent Hub – Conversational analytics, automated reporting and business intelligence. Category Management Agent Hub – Pricing, promotions, assortment, shelf and consumer intelligence. A key focus is the supervised agentic modelling approach, which combines AI-assisted analytical workflows with statistical modelling, model diagnostics and human validation. The paper proposes a conceptual framework connecting enterprise data integration, predictive intelligence, specialized AI agents, human oversight and operational decision-making. It also discusses the opportunities and challenges associated with enterprise AI adoption, including data quality, model explainability, statistical reliability, governance and organizational readiness. This publication is a conceptual research paper and industry case analysis based on academic literature and publicly available company information. Company-reported outcomes are identified as such and have not been independently verifie

latest.title: Financial Information Systems and their Role in Achieving Financial Sustainability An Analytical Study of the Opinions of a Sample of Employees in Commercial Banks
latest.abstract: Abstract. This study aims to analyze the role and dimensions of financial information systems (FIS) in achieving the financial sustainability of commercial banks. The researcher analyzed data from a questionnaire distributed to 250 employees of commercial banks. Based on rigorous scientific principles, the analysis focused on how FIS impacts the financial sustainability of these banks. The study sought to determine the relationship and correlation between FIS (the independent variable) and financial sustainability (the dependent variable). To achieve this, the researchers used SPSS and Amos V25 software. The results, collected through a specially designed questionnaire, revealed a correlation and influence between the dimensions of the independent variable (such as user efficiency, internal controls, hardware and software, system security, and senior management policies) and financial sustainability. One of the most important recommendations is to provide material and non-material incentives to employees in economic institutions, whether they are internal auditors or users of FIS, to enhance their sense of responsibility and encourage them to recognize the importance of their role within the organization

latest.title: Leakage-resistant graph learning for risk propagation and risk-constrained control in construction supply networks
latest.abstract: Introduction Construction supply network decisions require both predecision warning from information available before operations unfold and topology-aware diagnosis after the disruption context becomes visible. We introduce an auditable framework that separates these regimes through a strict start-of-week information contract and connects risk scores to safety-gated resource allocation. Methods We combined public SUCCESS construction-logistics records with a frozen queue-flow mechanism producing paired counterfactual outcomes on a heterogeneous network with 302 nodes and 1,277 edges. Models were trained on pilots A and B, selected on pilot C, and evaluated on pilot D. The strict contract excluded all week-t outcomes, service levels, and shock-source indicators. Complementary evaluations comprised context-aware diagnosis, a construction consolidation center (CCC) outage panel, leave-one-project-out evaluation, and an independent SupplyGraph boundary test. Six resource policies were compared through validation-only selection and a held-out Pareto audit. Results Under the strict contract, the graph convolutional network achieved the highest held-out area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.2397 and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8161 for 4,252 node-weeks with 60 positives. In the context-aware regime, relational GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5702, exceeding the matched multilayer perceptron (MLP) by 0.0803. Across eight positive pairs involving CCC outages, GraphSAGE achieved an AUPRC of 0.5845 versus 0.4994 for the MLP, with a positive pair-specific advantage in each case. The calibrated-risk guardrail identified an aggregate service improvement of 0.827% but screened the allocation out because the affected sites and failu

latest.title: When the algorithm feels like mine: personalisation depth, algorithmic transparency and psychological ownership in continued streaming engagement
latest.venue: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) personalisation depth and algorithmic transparency relate to continued engagement with streaming platforms through consumers’ psychological ownership of the recommendation stream, and over what range of privacy concern the transparency route holds. Design/methodology/approach A 14-day, two-wave panel of streaming subscribers in Türkiye (N = 450) was analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and re-estimated with covariance-based SEM. A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 236) manipulated both features. Findings Personalisation depth showed an indirect-only mediation pattern through ownership in the estimated model, with a direct path practically equivalent to zero within a pre-specified bound; the pattern replicated under random assignment. Ownership carried 45 per cent of the association between transparency and engagement, and a direct path accounted for the rest. The transparency–ownership link was no longer significant above a privacy-concern level of about 4.5 (7-point scale), a region holding roughly two in five respondents. Platform involvement strengthened the personalisation route; no group difference was detected for transparency. Research limitations/implications Participants were subscribers aged 18–35 in three Turkish cities, engagement was self-reported and ownership and engagement were measured on the same occasion. Practical implications Ownership measures can complement viewing and churn metrics when personalisation is evaluated, and layered explanations let users choose how much detail they see.
