latest.title: La influencia de las redes sociales en los casos de violencia juvenil: una aproximación criminológica desde la teoría de la imitación de Gabriel Tarde y la asociación diferencial de Edwin H. Sutherland
latest.venue: Ibero Ciencias - Revista Científica y Académica
latest.abstract: In recent years, digital technologies have transformed the ways young people interact, as they find social media to be new spaces for communication, identity construction, the development of a sense of belonging, and group integration. However, these same digital spaces can also facilitate the expansion of various expressions of youth violence, such as cyberbullying, the spread of violent content, symbolic violence, the promotion of aggressive behaviors, and the reproduction of discriminatory discourses. The objective of this work is to analyze the influence of social media on manifestations of youth violence from a criminological perspective. To this end, a narrative literature review of scientific work on digital violence, social learning, and youth behavior was conducted as part of a qualitative documentary research project. This review links the selected studies to two classic criminological theories: the theory of imitation developed by Gabriel Tarde and the theory of differential association proposed by Edwin H. Sutherland, aiming to understand how their approaches contribute to interpreting these manifestations of violence in digital environments.

latest.title: Pengaruh Daya Tarik dan Interaksi Parasosial Virtual Influencer Arbie Seo terhadap Minat Beli Produk Richeese Factory di Kalangan Gen Z Kota Semarang
latest.abstract: The growth of social media has encouraged the use of virtual influencers as part of digital marketing communication strategies. One such virtual influencer, Arbie SEO, serves as a brand ambassador for Richeese Factory. This study aims to examine the influence of the attractiveness and parasocial interaction of the virtual influencer Arbie SEO on the purchase intention for Richeese Factory products among Generation Z in Semarang City, both partially and simultaneously. The study employs a quantitative, explanatory approach. The sample consists of 100 Generation Z respondents in Semarang City, selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected via a questionnaire using a Likert scale and analyzed through multiple linear regression. The results indicate that the attractiveness of the virtual influencer Arbie SEO has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, with a t-value of 4.308 and a significance level of 0.000. Conversely, parasocial interaction does not have a significant effect on purchase intention, with a t-value of 1.277 and a significance level of 0.205. Simultaneously, both attractiveness and parasocial interaction have a significant effect on purchase intention, with an F-value of 73.265 and a significance level of 0.000. An R-squared value of 0.602 indicates that these two variables account for 60.2% of the variation in purchase intention, while the remaining 39.8% is explained by factors outside the scope of this study. The Theory of Planned Behavior remains relevant as a grand theory for providing the conceptual framework for this research.

latest.title: From orchestrated resources to supply chain performance: the indirect role of power
latest.abstract: Purpose The study applied resource orchestration and resource dependency theories to examine how firm resources affect supply chain performance in Ghana's food and beverage industry, as well as the mediating role of power. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach and explanatory design were employed using survey data collected from firms in Ghana's food and beverage sector. Out of the 427 questionnaires distributed, 395 usable responses were obtained. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling to assess direct and specific indirect effects. Findings The results indicate that human, financial and innovation resources significantly enhance supply chain performance, whereas relational and structural resources do not exert direct effects. Power positively influences performance and serves as a critical mechanism, with both partial and full mediation observed across resource categories. The findings reveal that resource value is heterogeneous and context-dependent, and that performance gains are realised when resources are effectively translated into influence that aligns with partner behaviour. Originality/value The study advances the literature by moving beyond the composite view of firm resources and demonstrating that resource effects are not uniform but context-specific. It further positions power as a central mechanism linking resource deployment to performance, offering a more context-sensitive explanation of supply chain dynamics in developing economies.

latest.title: ENVIRONMENTAL CLEANLINESS AND PERCEIVED WORKOUT EXPERIENCES: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF JK DIVERSION AND LIBONGAO DIVERSION IN KANANGA, LEYTE
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between environmental cleanliness and perceived workout experiences in two recreational areas, JK Diversion and Libongao Diversion, in the Municipality of Kananga, Leyte, Philippines. It specifically explores how users perceive the cleanliness of these locations, their reported comfort while engaging in physical activities, and whether environmental cleanliness influences their willingness to use recreational spaces. A quantitative comparative research design with a correlational component was employed, involving 100 respondents, with 50 participants from each recreational area. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire covering three key aspects: perceived environmental cleanliness, comfort during workouts, and the influence of cleanliness on willingness to use recreational areas. Descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank-order correlation, and the chi-square test of independence were used to analyze the responses. The findings revealed a substantial difference in perceived cleanliness between the two locations. All respondents from JK Diversion agreed that the area was clean, while 98% of respondents from Libongao Diversion disagreed. Despite this difference, positive responses regarding workout comfort were relatively similar between the locations, at 54% and 48%, respectively. Statistical analysis did not establish a significant association between perceived cleanliness and reported workout comfort (Spearman's ρ = 0.011, p = 0.910). Similarly, the difference in workout comfort responses between the two locations was not statistically significant (χ² = 1.158, p = 0.560). Nevertheless, 97% of all respondents agreed or strongly agreed that cleanliness influences their willingness to use recreational areas. This research c

latest.title: Beyond the basics: how digital transformation, orientation and competence fuel SME performance through resilience in the manufacturing sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
latest.abstract: Purpose In emerging economies such as Pakistan, SMEs have a high failure rate, underscoring the need to understand what drives SME performance. This paper fills a knowledge gap by considering the impact of digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and entrepreneurial resilience on SMEs' performance. Entrepreneurial resilience serves as a mediator between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, environmental dynamism (ED) is used as a moderator between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 453 managers of manufacturing SMEs in Punjab, Pakistan. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling is used for hypothesis testing. Findings Digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation and entrepreneurial competencies have a significant and positive influence on entrepreneurial resilience and SME performance. Entrepreneurial resilience significantly enhances SMEs' performance. Additionally, entrepreneurial resilience significantly mediates the relationships among digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, ED significantly moderates the relationship between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Practical implications SME managers should prioritize digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, competence, resilience and ED to measure SMEs' performance. Policymakers can support these efforts by developing adaptive frameworks that enable SMEs to remain competitive in dynamic environments. Originality/value This is initial research that integrates digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial

latest.title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
latest.abstract: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

latest.title: Childhood Trauma and APOEε4 Are Associated With Patterns of Developmental Frontal Alpha Connectivity, Posttraumatic Stress, and Alcohol‐Related Outcomes
latest.abstract: Childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of APOEε4, the genetic factor most associated with Alzheimer's disease. Longitudinal studies of APOEε4, childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. We studied 837 trauma-exposed participants (53% female) from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and APOEε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha EEG coherence (EEGc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. Young adult AUD and PTSD symptoms were also examined. Results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (CSAT) and APOEε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. CSAT was associated with a higher EEGc baseline but less growth in three EEGc pairs, while APOEε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (LFC) EEGc baseline and higher slope. EEGc patterns and symptoms of PTSD and AUD were robustly associated. A significant interaction between CSAT-by-APOEε4 interaction also emerged, such that among APOEε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline PFI and diminished growth in PFI and LFC EEGc. No significant direct links between APOEε4 and PTSD or AUD were observed. Findings highlight how EEGc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at-risk group identification and informing prevention strategies.

latest.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
latest.abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

latest.title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
latest.abstract: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

latest.title: Does Efficient Morphological Decoding Explain Unique Variance in the Reading Abilities of Middle School Students?
latest.abstract: Does Automatic Morphological Processing Uniquely Contribute to the Reading Abilities of Middle School Students?Purpose: Morphological processing is theorized to contribute to skilled reading via the processing of high-level regularities (e.g., semantics). However, morphemes also may contribute to skilled reading via relatively low-level regularities: orthography and phonology. Evidence suggests that middle school marks the shift from effortful use of knowledge of morphological structure during word reading to its automatic activation, thus supporting the development of reading fluency and comprehension. Consequently, this study asked whether automatic morphological processing contributes unique variance to these reading outcomes in middle school students. Method: Participants were 80 seventh- and eighth-grade students (n female = 42, n male = 38; mean age = 12.76 years). Four assessments measured decoding, oral reading fluency, and comprehension. Four computer-administered experimental tasks (each with a masked and unmasked version) indexed automaticity and knowledge in reading morphologically complex and simple words. Three analysis approaches were used in a conceptual replication of previous studies (Roembke et al., 2019; 2021): mixed ANOVAs, commonality analyses, and hierarchical regressions.Results: Only automaticity with morphologically complex words contributed unique variance to comprehension, and it also contributed unique variance to fluency. This was shown on a task that required the mapping of morpho-orthographic to morpho-phonological regularities. Automaticity with morphologically simple words most consistently contributed unique variance to decoding and fluency. Conclusions: Results suggest that middle school students automatically apply morpho-orthographi

latest.title: Effect of Contemplative Monastic Debate Practice on Emotion Regulation and Experience
latest.abstract: In this study, we set out to examine whether Monastic Debate practice can help with emotion regulation and reduce the experience of negative affect. Research on traditional contemplative practices—including mindfulness, loving-kindness meditation, and yoga—shows that they influence emotion regulation and emotional experience. However, systematic reasoning, appraisal, and emotion regulation in a social context are not usually part of these practices. Here, we investigated another contemplative practice called Monastic Debate , a Buddhist practice based purely on logic and reasoning that follows stringent rules established by Indian and later Tibetan masters. Monastic Debate is a practice in which the practitioner seeks to improve their understanding of Buddhist philosophy by engaging in a precisely described process of reasoning in interaction with one or more others. We recruited novice practitioners (non-monks) from a month-long winter debate retreat. During the experiment, participants completed the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS) and the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS). We observed a significant reduction in difficulty regulating emotions in our retreat group compared to the control group. Particularly, four subscales of DERS, namely nonacceptance, impulse, strategies, and goals, showed a significant reduction for the retreat group in comparison to the control group. We did not observe any significant differences in positive or negative emotional experiences between the retreat and control groups. The results suggest that the logical ability developed in a non-monastic population by participating in a 1-month Monastic Debate practice can help improve the ability to regulate emotions.

latest.title: Age-related amplification of spatial contextual influence on visual scene processing.
latest.abstract: Older adults rely increasingly on prior knowledge to make sense of their deteriorating representation of the visual world, but how this shapes scene perception and spatial reorientation remains unclear. To address this issue, 28 young and 25 older adults viewed artificially generated rooms either before or after learning the position of a goal hidden in an adjacent room. We manipulated both the number and the eccentricity of navigational affordances (i.e., open doors) to investigate the interaction between bottom-up scene features and top-down spatial knowledge. Consistent with previous findings, younger adults showed decreased performance as the number of open doors increased, but only after learning the goal position, indicating a top-down interaction with the automatic processing of affordances. Door eccentricity did not affect this interaction, suggesting our findings were not due to a distractor effect. In older adults, this interaction between prior spatial information and navigational affordances was markedly amplified: reaction times increased at twice the rate observed in younger adults. These findings show that prior spatial knowledge interacts with the automatic extraction of navigational affordances, and that this influence is markedly amplified with age. While prior knowledge helps stabilize perception when sensory processing becomes less reliable, it can also increase the processing time for complex scenes, particularly when multiple action possibilities are present. By revealing how aging shifts the balance between top-down and bottom-up mechanisms, these results refine models of age-related spatial navigation decline and highlight a trade-off whereby increased reliance on prior knowledge supports perception but can also slow interaction with complex envi

latest.title: Music exposure reduces anxiety- and depression-like behavior in rodents: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis
latest.abstract: Abstract Anxiety and depressive disorders impose a major global burden, prompting interest in non-pharmacological interventions that may influence affective processes. Music exposure has often been reported to affect anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, but preclinical findings remain heterogeneous and have not been quantitatively synthesized. Prior work has also focused almost entirely on mean behavioral responses, largely overlooking inter-individual variability as a biologically meaningful dimension. We conducted a preregistered systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of experimental studies testing music exposure in laboratory rodents. Following PRISMA and PRISMA-EcoEvo guidelines, we synthesized 298 effect sizes from 20 studies using multilevel models to account for non-independence among effect sizes. We quantified effects on mean behavior with the log response ratio (ln RR ) and effects on variability with the log variability ratio (ln V R ). Overall, music exposure was associated with a statistically significant reduction in anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, corresponding to an average decrease of about 18% relative to controls. This mean effect was detected across outcome types and life stages despite substantial heterogeneity. By contrast, music exposure did not produce a statistically significant overall change in inter-individual behavioral variability. Instead, variability responses were context dependent: behavioral assay type and music meta-genre significantly moderated ln V R , with anxiety-like assays tending to show increased variability and depression-like assays tending to show reduced variability under music exposure. These results suggest that music exposure reliably shifts average affect-related behavior without uniformly changing

latest.title: What is compassion connected to, and does it differ by gender and age? A network analysis of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy and mental health
latest.abstract: Abstract Compassion is an emotional state experienced in response to witnessing the suffering of others, accompanied by an internal motivation to help. When directed toward the self, it is referred to as self-compassion. Previous research suggests that compassion and self-compassion are closely related to mindfulness and empathy, contributing to reductions in anxiety and depression and to the enhancement of positive affect. Accordingly, this study employed network analysis to explore the complex structure of interactions among these psychological variables. A total of 1,020 Korean adults completed measures of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy, well-being, and negative affect (depression, anxiety, and stress). An EBICglasso network was estimated in R (version 4.5.1). Centrality indices were computed, and subgroup networks were constructed by gender and age to compare structural differences. The results showed that compassion was closely connected to empathy, whereas self-compassion was more strongly linked to mindfulness and well-being; the capacities to feel, tolerate, and alleviate suffering emerged as central nodes. In the gender-based networks, compassion and self-compassion among men tended to be organized primarily around cognitive factors, whereas women exhibited a pattern in which the behavioral motivation for compassion was activated relatively immediately, even in the absence of emotional responding. In the age-based networks, the influence of suffering tolerance was most pronounced in middle-aged adults, while the role of empathy diminished and the role of mindfulness expanded in older adults. By examining compassion at the level of its constituent elements and visualizing the interaction structure among related variables, this study provides a

latest.title: Data analytics capabilities and organisational performance at an emerging economy’s local government assembly: the roles of top-management support and data driven decision making
latest.abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of Data Analytics Capability on organisational performance within an emerging economy’s local government assembly, with particular focus on the mediating role of Data-Driven Decision Making and the influence of Top Management Support. Grounded in the Organisational Information Processing Theory and the Upper Echelons Theory, the study adopts a cross-sectional survey explanatory design. Data was collected from 127 employees of the local assembly through structured online questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structured Equation Modelling. The results reveal that DAC has no significant direct effect on organisational performance but exerts a strong positive effect on DDDM. In turn, DDDM significantly enhances organisational performance and mediates the relationship between DAC and performance. Additionally, TMS support significantly and directly influences organisational performance, although it does not moderate the DAC-performance relationship. The study concludes that DAC alone do not guarantee improved performance, rather, their value is realized through integration into decision-making processes. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to provide empirical evidence from an emerging economy’s local government context demonstrating that DDDM is the critical pathway through which DAC translate into performance outcomes, while TMS operates as a direct driver rather than a conditional enhancer. This study contributes theoretically by refining the application of the OIPT and the UET in public sector analytics contexts and offers practical insights that performance improvements depend more on the use of data in decision-making than on the mere possession of analytics infrastructure.

latest.title: Conceptualizing carbon accounting disclosure and firm performance under sustainability committee oversight in Malaysian oil and gas industry
latest.abstract: Abstract In the growing global warming crisis, firms operating in high carbon-intensive industries like the Oil and Gas (O&G) sector are focusing on carbon reduction and transparency. However, Carbon Accounting Disclosure (CAD) in emerging economies, such as Malaysia, remains voluntary and non-standardized, which reduces its effectiveness for firm sustainable performance. To address this gap, this study proposes the Sustainability Committee (SC)-Moderated CAD Framework to examine the effect of monetary and non-monetary CAD on firm’s financial and ESG performance, with the moderating role of SC among Malaysian O&G companies listed on Bursa Malaysia. Based on stakeholder and legitimacy theories for direct relationships, and agency theory for the moderating role, the model uses a weighted disclosure index to measure CAD aspects. It is expected that different types of CAD has a positive impact on firm performance, with an effective SC strengthening this relationship by minimizing information asymmetry and promoting improved environmental practices. This study is expected to contribute to the literature by differentiating between monetary and non-monetary CAD and theorizing the potential moderating role of the SC. Furthermore, it offers policy recommendations for policymakers in advancing Malaysia’s Net-Zero emissions target by 2050 through strengthened green governance and the adoption of mandatory sustainability reporting.

latest.title: Field-based correlates of total 505 change-of-direction test time in 9 to 10 year old children: an exploratory cross-sectional study
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Field based physical fitness tests are widely used to describe motor performance in school age children, but the motor and anthropometric correlates of change of direction tasks during late childhood remain incompletely described. The 505 change of direction (COD) test captures a pre planned movement task that requires acceleration, deceleration, turning, and reacceleration. This study examined motor performance and field based physical fitness correlates of 505 COD performance in 9 to 10 year old children. Methods This exploratory cross-sectional study included 98 apparently healthy school age children (55 boys and 43 girls). The 505 COD time was used as the outcome variable. Candidate field based variables included 20 m sprint time, back leg strength, handgrip strength, squat jump, simple visual reaction time, flexibility tests, and selected anthropometric indices. Sex stratified correlations were interpreted with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) q values. Exploratory regression models were intentionally conservative and should be interpreted as within sample explanatory models rather than validated prediction tools. Results Across boys and girls, 20 m sprint time was the most consistent correlate of 505 COD time. In boys, the model including 20 m sprint time and back leg strength explained 39.8% of the variance in 505 COD time (adjusted R2 = 0.375). In girls, the conservative model including 20 m sprint time and simple visual reaction time explained 58.9% of the variance (adjusted R2 = 0.568). A sensitivity model including shoulder hip ratio explained 63.3% of the variance but was interpreted cautiously because shoulder hip ratio was not a significant bivariate correlate of 505 COD time. Conclusions In school age children, linear spri

latest.title: Prevalence and association of adverse childhood experiences among voluntarily-admitted substance use disorder inpatients in Thailand
latest.abstract: Abstract Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are increasingly recognized as an important driver of the global substance use disorder (SUD) issue. However, current literature regarding this topic contains limited knowledge from Asia-Pacific countries and hardly any research from Thailand. Therefore, this study sought to examine the prevalence and impact of ACEs among SUD inpatients in Thailand. In this cross-sectional study, 249 individuals with SUD recruited from Northern Thailand’s specialist drug and alcohol hospital’s In-Patient Department completed the ACE Questionnaire (Thai-version) and the Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST). The prevalence of high ACE scores (≥ 4) and of each individual ACE category were calculated, with 95% confidence intervals estimated using the Wald method. Binary logistic regression was used to explore the relationship between ACEs and high-risk substance use. The prevalence of high ACE scores in this group was 23.7% (95%CI 18.4–29.0%). High prevalence was also observed across every single ACE category. High ACE scores were associated with high-risk polysubstance use (AOR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02–3.50, p = 0.044), high-risk depressant use (AOR = 1.86, 95%CI 1.01–3.46, p = 0.048), and high-risk cannabis use (AOR = 2.73, 95%CI 1.16–6.39, p = 0.021) after adjusting for age, sex, and level of education. However, no statistically significant association was found between high ACE scores and high-risk stimulant use. Among SUD inpatients in Thailand, ACEs are highly prevalent and significantly associated with high-risk substance use. These findings underscore the necessity for trauma-informed drug policies and the value of ACEs-SUD research in understudied countries.

latest.title: Initial examination of the Need for Chaos (Revised) Scale in German
latest.abstract: The term need for chaos refers to an individual’s mindset demonstrating a desire for the destruction of the established order and the societal structures. This novel construct may be of relevance for forensic, legal, and safety matters as well as politics. To measure differences in individuals’ need for chaos, the seven-items NFCChaos Scale was developed in English. Later two items were added to create the recently proposed nine-items NFCChaos-R Scale. In the present study (N = 817), we present German adaptations of the two scales and an initial examination of their psychometric properties. For the German seven-items NFCChaos Scale, we found a two-dimensional structure with the factors enjoyment of destruction and chaos seeking for rebuilding which were strongly and positively interrelated. The data also suggest that the two additional items of the German nine-items NFCChaos-R Scale capture yet another construct (i.e., lacking desire for order). Furthermore, results preliminary indicate sufficient reliability and validity of the German adaptations. Dark personality measures (e.g., dark core, psychopathy), left-wing authoritarian anti-hierarchical aggression, radicalism intention (i.e., the intention to use illegal and violent means for political ends), and the inclination to justify political violence emerged as substantial correlates of the need for chaos in our German-speaking sample.

latest.title: Market Structure and Export Competitiveness in the Global Mango Trade: An HHI, CMS and RSCA Approach (2006–2024)
latest.abstract: Abstract The present study investigates the competitiveness of the global fresh mango market from 2006 to 2024. HHI scores between 673.75 and 848.18 indicate a high level of competition and market diversification, rather than a monopoly. The CMS analysis reveals that Thailand recorded a positive value of 578,997 tons, while India recorded a negative value of -661,383 tons. In 2024, Peru and Pakistan had scores between 0.86 and 0.95, while India's score decreased sharply from 0.90 in 2006 to 0.35 in 2024. The results of the econometric models for 16 countries show that Agricultural Productivity positively affects overall market competitiveness (β = 0.351; p < 0.001), while Import Unit value Index negatively affects overall market competitiveness (β = -0.353; p < 0.001). A hybrid strategy, however, was effective in boosting competitiveness in Spain even as import prices rose (β = 0.525; p = 0.038), as indicated by country-specific models. The results confirm that quality leadership, value-added products, and market diversification are not only important for achieving economies of scale and bulk production, but also for sustaining a competitive advantage.

latest.title: Sleep duration, depressive symptoms, and memory aging: longitudinal patterns and temporal network evidence from four-wave CHARLS study (2011–2018)
latest.abstract: Sleep is a modifiable behavioral factor closely linked to cognitive aging and depressive symptoms. However, evidence remains limited on whether nocturnal sleep and midday nap duration are nonlinearly associated with heterogeneous longitudinal patterns of subjective memory complaints (SMCs), objective episodic memory (OEM), and depressive symptoms, as well as their temporal interrelationships. We analyzed four-wave data (2011–2018) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 7,198 participants aged ≥ 45 years (mean age: 56.12 ± 7.93 years; 51.8% female). Sleep duration was self-reported. SMCs, OEM (Word Recall Test, reverse-coded), and depressive symptoms (CESD-10) were assessed. K-means clustering was applied to identify longitudinal patterns of SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms. Restricted cubic spline models were applied to examine potential nonlinear dose–response associations between sleep duration and longitudinal patterns. Cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis was used to examine the temporal and directional associations among these variables across waves. Distinct longitudinal patterns were identified for SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms. Sleep duration showed nonlinear associations with trajectories reflecting poorer memory outcomes and greater depressive symptoms, with estimated nadirs of approximately 7.6, 6.9, and 7.7 h for SMCs, OEM, and depressive symptoms, respectively. CLPN analysis demonstrated stable network structures with good centrality stability. SMCs showed the highest out-expected influence, while OEM demonstrated the highest in-expected influence, suggesting a consistent cross-wave predictive association from SMCs to subsequent OEM scores. Deviations from the nocturnal sleep duration at the estimated nadir

latest.title: VAT Treatment of Core Crypto Transactions in the System of EU VAT and Beyond
latest.abstract: Transactions in virtual crypto assets challenge VAT systems that were designed for conventional business models. With a particular focus on the common system of EU VAT, this article examines the treatment of core crypto transactions involving payment tokens, NFTs and utility tokens. It argues that crypto assets cannot be classified generically for VAT purposes. Instead, their treatment depends on the technological design of the relevant blockchain mechanism and the economic function of the token. The analysis addresses VAT issues related to mining and staking, trading in primary and secondary markets, the use of tokens, and the services provided by portal and interface operators. It includes an assessment of deemed supplier regimes for crypto platforms, margin schemes, and a special regime for vouchers from a VAT law and policy perspective. The article further shows that crypto pseudonymity creates particular difficulties for applying the destination principle, determining the taxable amount, and enforcing VAT liabilities, and presents possible solutions. The article thereby identifies the key issues that need to be addressed by any VAT/GST system to ensure adequate, neutral and efficient taxation of crypto assets.

latest.title: Improving the Competitiveness Management Mechanism of Service Enterprises
latest.venue: Academic Journal of Digital Economics and Stability
latest.abstract: This article analyzes issues related to improving the mechanism for managing the competitiveness of service enterprises. The role of the service sector in the national economy, its share in the gross domestic product, and its importance in economic development are scientifically examined. In addition, the factors influencing the increase of competitiveness of service enterprises, the ways of effectively organizing management mechanisms, and the development trends of the service market in modern economic conditions are considered.

latest.title: From Online Engagement to Heritage Visits: Mapping Consumer Pathways in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tourism
latest.abstract: This study investigates how heritage sites in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) are portrayed through digital storytelling across various online platforms and how these narratives influence the cyber-customer path in tourism decision-making. Using qualitative content analysis, the research examines 40 digital media artifacts including Instagram posts, YouTube travel vlogs, tourism blogs, and official promotional websites to identify how different stages of the cyber-customer journey (awareness, interest, evaluation, decision, and advocacy) are represented in the content. The study discloses that platforms like Instagram and YouTube use highly visual and emotional storytelling to create initial awareness and interest, while blogs and official websites provide evaluative content that supports travel decisions. Key stakeholders in these narratives include influencers, government tourism bodies, and travel communities. The research highlights digital media’s significant role in shaping heritage perceptions, encouraging responsible tourism, and connecting audiences to cultural narratives through engaging formats. The findings contribute to media studies and heritage tourism by providing a model for analysing the intersection of storytelling, tourism behaviour, and digital media strategy.

latest.title: Влияние социальных сетей на международный маркетинг
latest.abstract: В статье исследуется трансформация инструментария международного маркетинга под влиянием глобальных социальных платформ. Рассмотрены ключевые барьеры адаптации маркетинговых стратегий при выходе брендов на зарубежные рынки, включая кросс-культурные различия, правовые ограничения и региональную специфику алгоритмов дистрибуции контента. На основе анализа метрик вовлеченности, стоимости привлечения клиента и возврата инвестиций определена эффективная структура распределения ресурсов между глобальными и локальными каналами коммуникации. Выявлена зависимость показателей конверсии от степени интеграции микроинфлюенсеров в локальные маркетинговые кампании.

latest.title: Influence of AI personalization on consumer loyalty in the restaurant business: balance between efficiency and ethics
latest.abstract: The article examines the influence of artificial intelligence-based personalization on the formation of consumer loyalty in the restaurant business. Current trends in the implementation of AI tools, including recommendation systems, dynamic pricing, and loyalty programs, as well as their impact on customer experience, are analyzed. Based on an analysis of empirical data and scholarly publications, key factors determining the effectiveness of AI personalization are identified: relevance of offers, transparency of data use, and preservation of «human» contact. Particular attention is paid to ethical aspects - issues of privacy, risks of dehumanization of service, and manipulative influence on consumer choice. A model for balanced implementation of AI personalization is proposed, taking into account both economic efficiency and ethical constraints. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of applying the proposed recommendations in forming digital transformation strategies for restaurant enterprises.

latest.title: Асимметрия ценообразования на российском рынке кондитерских изделий
latest.abstract: В статье исследуется асимметрия ценообразования на отечественном рынке кондитерской продукции. На фоне глобального падения цены на какао бобы индексы цен производителей на готовую продукцию в России до 2026 г. продолжали расти. Проведенный сравнительный анализ динамики тарифов на электроэнергию и грузовые перевозки показал, что эти затраты не являлись основными в увеличении стоимости кондитерских изделий при ценообразовании. Авторы отмечают, что на сегодняшний день рынок находится под влиянием различных факторов, вызывающих дисбаланс в ценообразовании кондитерской продукции. Даже в условиях стабилизации сырьевого рынка асимметрия ценообразования проявляется в запоздании переноса затрат; отсутствии у производителей стимула к снижению конечной цены при уменьшении стоимости сырья; разнице скорости перерасчета цен при выходе на внешний рынок, а также во влиянии неценовых факторов.

latest.title: Adaptive omnichannel brand management architecture for light industry enterprises: from brand identity to performance control
latest.abstract: The article substantiates an integrated approach to brand management in light industry enterprises under conditions of digitalization, changing consumer behavior, and increasing fragmentation of interaction channels. Brand management is interpreted as an organizational and functional subsystem that ensures the alignment of strategic positioning, brand identity, communications, digital and physical touchpoints, and analytical control. A three-layer omnichannel brand-management architecture is proposed, comprising the strategic and identity core, the omnichannel interaction layer, and the performance-control layer. The functional content of the system is structured around four interrelated blocks: strategic planning, design, communications, and analytics. Particular attention is paid to the coordination of websites and mobile interfaces, marketplaces, social media, and physical retail within a unified customer journey. The performance-control layer links consumer response, conversion, loyalty, channel efficiency, and economic results, thereby closing the management loop. A recurrent adaptive management cycle is proposed, including diagnosis, identification of structural imbalance, selection of managerial intervention, implementation, measurement, and adjustment. The proposed approach makes it possible to identify structural bottlenecks in brand management and to select differentiated managerial actions aimed at strengthening brand coherence, continuity of customer experience, and market effectiveness.

latest.title: Staff turnover: its nature, factors and management approaches
latest.abstract: Staff stability largely determines organisational performance, while high rates of employee departures create additional organisational and economic challenges. The article examines the nature of staff turnover and identifies the main factors influencing its level. Based on a review of existing academic approaches, a classification of staff turnover factors is proposed, comprising financial, organisational and work-related, professional and career-related, socio-psychological, individual and external factors. Particular attention is paid to the consequences of employee departures for organisations and the possibilities of preventing undesirable turnover. The study demonstrates that the selection of employee retention measures should take account of the specific reasons for leaving, as applying the same measures in all cases does not adequately reflect differences in employees' work motivation and expectations. The main approaches to managing staff turnover are identified, including improvements in remuneration and work organisation, employee induction and adaptation, professional development, career advancement and internal communication.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Доверие как психотерапевтический фактор и детерминанта удовлетворённости браком в молодой семье
latest.abstract: Статья посвящена исследованию феномена доверия как системного психотерапевтического фактора и ключевой детерминанты удовлетворенности браком в молодой семье. В работе раскрыта многомерная структура доверия, включающая эмоциональный, когнитивный и поведенческий компоненты, а также проанализирована трансформация его функций на различных этапах жизненного цикла молодой пары (от первичной адаптации до периода стабилизации системы). Рассмотрены механизмы влияния взаимного доверия на снижение межличностной тревожности, оптимизацию ролевого взаимодействия и профилактику супружеских конфликтов. Особое внимание уделено психотерапевтическому потенциалу доверия в контексте семейного консультирования. В рамках исследования разработаны фазово-целевая модель восстановления доверия и систематизированы психотерапевтические методы (инструментарий эмоционально-фокусированной, когнитивно-поведенческой и системной семейной психотерапии), направленные на преодоление деструктивных паттернов взаимодействия и травм привязанности. Сформулированы эмпирические закономерности, подтверждающие медиативную роль доверия в обеспечении психологической устойчивости и благополучия супружеских отношений.

latest.title: New employee adaptation in human resource management
latest.abstract: New employee adaptation is an important component of human resource management and largely determines how employees adjust to a new working environment. The article examines professional, organisational and socio-psychological aspects of adaptation, as well as the main difficulties employees encounter after joining an organisation. The relationship between the adaptation process, job satisfaction and staff turnover is analysed. A model illustrating the influence of adaptation on new employee retention is proposed, taking into account adaptation conditions, its main aspects, intermediate outcomes and possible consequences. The article also considers adaptation tools and the specific features of their application depending on the difficulties experienced by new employees.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Развитие межличностных отношений современных младших школьников
latest.abstract: Статья посвящена актуальной проблеме развития межличностных отношений у младших школьников в условиях цифровизации общества. В статье раскрыта актуальность изучения межличностных отношений в младшем школьном возрасте с учётом современных социальных тенденций; проанализированы ключевые проблемы развития межличностных отношений у современных младших школьников: снижение способности к конструктивному общению, эмоциональный дефицит, трудности в построении дружеских отношений, искажение ценностных ориентиров; представлена теоретическая база исследования, опирающаяся на концепции В. Н. Мясищева, Б. Г. Ананьева, Е. П. Ильина, А. Н. Леонтьева, Л. С. Выготского и других учёных; обоснована целесообразность использования игрового тренинга как психолого-педагогического инструмента развития межличностных отношений; предложен геймифицированный подход к организации игровых тренингов, сочетающий традиционные игровые формы с элементами геймификации. Охарактеризованы три компонента межличностных отношений, развитие которых возможно через геймифицированные тренинги: когнитивный – усвоение правил и норм социального взаимодействия; аффективный – развитие эмпатии и умения распознавать эмоции; поведенческий – формирование навыков взаимодействия со сверстниками. В работе подробно описаны психологические и педагогические механизмы воздействия геймификации, эмотиконов и мемов на развитие межличностных отношений, приведены примеры игровых упражнений для каждого компонента. Научная новизна исследования заключается в комплексном подходе к развитию межличностных отношений младших школьников через интеграцию традиционных игровых методов и современных цифровых элементов в рамках геймифицированных тренингов. Практическая значимость состоит в возможности применения предложенных методик педагогами и псих

latest.title: Integrated diagnostics of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail
latest.abstract: The article develops an integrated diagnostic model of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail aimed at identifying imbalances between technological development, organizational capabilities, and market outcomes. The proposed approach combines four interrelated diagnostic contours: external digital opportunities, actual technology adoption, internal digital readiness, and customer and market response. The research is based on system, process, comparative, and structural-logical approaches, as well as analysis, synthesis, classification, and scientific generalization. The empirical illustration of the model uses publicly available corporate data for 2025-2026 covering ten Russian FMCG retail chains. Digital readiness is assessed through four components: management commitment, digital potential, digital culture, and digital strategy. The results indicate that relatively balanced average levels of digital readiness coexist with noticeable firm-level differences in their internal configuration. Digital culture demonstrates the highest average value (0.885), whereas digital strategy has the lowest (0.840), suggesting that the development of technological and organizational capabilities may outpace their integration into a coherent long-term transformation agenda. To translate diagnostic results into managerial decisions, a matrix linking specific diagnostic signals with corresponding management responses is proposed. The developed framework supports the identification of capability bottlenecks, underused technologies, customer-journey friction, and inconsistencies between digital readiness and actual technology adoption. Its practical application can facilitate the prioritization of digital initiatives, continuous monitoring, strategic adjustment, control, and recurren

latest.title: Личностный профиль родителя как предиктор развития креативности в дошкольном детстве: эмпирический анализ и практические стратегии
latest.abstract: В статье представлены результаты эмпирического исследования влияния личностных характеристик матерей на уровень креативности детей старшего дошкольного возраста. На выборке из 60 диад «мать и ребёнок» (возраст детей 5,5-6,5 лет) с применением корреляционного анализа (коэффициент Спирмена) выявлены значимые связи между параметрами «большой пятёрки», личностной тревожностью матерей и показателями дивергентного мышления дошкольников. Показано, что экспрессивность (r = 0.850; p < 0.001), эмпатийная привязанность (r = 0.810; p < 0.001) и социальная открытость (r = 0.841; p < 0.001) выступают фасилитаторами детского творчества, тогда как нейротизм (r = −0.837; p < 0.001), тревожность (r = −0.824; p < 0.001) и гиперсоциализированный самоконтроль (r = −0.813; p < 0.001) оказывают ингибирующее воздействие. Пол ребёнка не является значимым модератором выявленных связей. На основе полученных данных разработаны практические рекомендации для родителей и специалистов системы образования. Теоретическая значимость работы заключается в уточнении роли некогнитивных родительских характеристик в детском развитии.

latest.title: ИИ-инструменты как фактор оптимизации стратегии продвижения бренда одежды на маркетплейсах (на примере Wildberries)
latest.abstract: Статья посвящена анализу инструментов искусственного интеллекта как фактора оптимизации стратегии продвижения бренда одежды на маркетплейсах, с акцентом на специфику платформы Wildberries. Рассмотрены основные группы ИИ-инструментов (генеративные и аналитические) и раскрыт их вклад в оптимизацию карточки товара, ранжирование в поисковой выдаче маркетплейса, генерацию визуального и текстового контента, а также персонализацию коммуникации с покупателем на внешних каналах. Предложена трёхшаговая модель применения ИИ-инструментов при продвижении бренда одежды на Wildberries. Обозначены ограничения и риски использования генеративного ИИ в fashion-маркетинге, связанные с достоверностью визуализации товара, унификацией стиля брендов-конкурентов и вопросами интеллектуальной собственности.

latest.title: Contemporary approaches to fostering employee loyalty in organisations
latest.abstract: The article examines the theoretical aspects of employee loyalty within organisational management. Based on a synthesis of academic approaches, the concept and main characteristics of loyalty are explored, together with its manifestations in employment relationships. The factors influencing the development of employee loyalty are systematised, including working conditions, financial incentives, organisational culture, social relationships and opportunities for professional development. The main approaches to managing employee loyalty and methods of assessing it are also considered. The need for a comprehensive approach to developing and maintaining employee loyalty, taking into account organisational characteristics and employees’ professional needs, is substantiated.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: From Intention to Automaticity: Daily Evidence of Habit Formation in Students’ Everyday Lives
latest.abstract: Abstract Students’ recurring behaviors are central to academic, health, and well-being outcomes, yet educational psychology has placed less emphasis on habit formation than on motivation, metacognition, and deliberate self-regulation. This study used daily longitudinal data from a 10- to 12-week course-embedded habit project to test theoretically derived predictions about habit development in students’ everyday lives. Across five semesters, 175 students selected a habit they wanted to build and contributed 9,416 daily reports indicating whether they intended to enact the behavior, whether they did so, and how automatic the behavior felt. Students completed their selected behavior on 76.1% of intended days. Mixed-effects models supported two primary predictions: students reported stronger automaticity as they accumulated more prior repetitions, and stronger prior automaticity predicted a greater likelihood of completing the behavior on intended days. These patterns were robust across semesters and survey-completion thresholds. Secondary analyses suggested that weekends and spring break functioned as naturalistic disruptions, and success-profile analyses showed substantial variability in habit-formation outcomes across students. Together, the findings suggest that deliberate self-regulation and habit formation can operate as complementary processes: students selected and planned their behaviors, behaviors repeated more often felt more automatic, and behaviors that felt more automatic were more likely to be performed as intended. The study extends existing habit-formation evidence to students’ everyday academic, health, and well-being routines and supports more targeted future research on learning-related habits and educational outcomes.

latest.title: Interconnected Mental Health Stressors and Risks in Returnee Nepalese Migrant Workers: A Focus Group Study
latest.abstract: Abstract For Nepalese migrant workers, working abroad can negatively affect their mental health and well-being. Studies on labour migrants have documented poor occupational health outcomes, both mental and physical. However, research into their sources of stress, coping mechanisms, and suicidal thoughts remains limited. This qualitative study explored the sources of stress and perceived risks to mental health in returnee Nepalese migrant workers. We conducted seven focus groups (five male, one female and one mixed gender) with returnee migrants from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and Malaysia. Participants were purposively recruited with support from local health workers and community organisations working for migrants. Over half had worked abroad for at least five years, with an average of 7.7 years. Our analysis identified six themes: (1) accommodation and communication; (2) occupational health; (3) exploitation at work; (4) family at home; (5) leisure, coping and risk behaviours; and (6) suicide narratives and mental health support, all six are linked to social determinants of mental health. These interconnected themes can negatively impact the mental health and well-being of migrant workers. Gender disparities and limited mental health support available abroad, including suicide prevention strategies, further intensify these challenges. Since this study focuses on returnees, workers currently abroad might have different experiences. Overall, our findings underscore the need for targeted support and interventions to improve the mental health and well-being of Nepalese migrant workers. We recommend establishing longitudinal studies to inform policy and practice related to mental health.

latest.title: Pemanfaatan Microsoft Excel Dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) Perspektif Hukum Ekonomi Syariah
latest.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need orderly financial records to monitor business activities, assess performance, and make responsible economic decisions. For Muslim-owned or sharia-oriented MSMEs, financial administration also has a normative dimension: transactions should be recorded transparently, agreements should be clear, and business practices should avoid riba, gharar, and maysir. This article examines the use of Microsoft Excel in MSME financial management from the perspective of Islamic economic law. It applies a descriptive qualitative literature-review method combined with a normative-conceptual analysis of sharia business principles, relevant regulations, and studies on spreadsheet-based accounting and sharia-oriented MSMEs. The literature indicates that Excel can assist transaction recording, cash-flow monitoring, cost calculation, inventory control, and preparation of financial summaries. From an Islamic economic law perspective, these functions may support the principles of amanah, shiddiq, ‘adl, transparency, and protection of wealth (hifz al-mal), provided that the workbook records the substance of transactions accurately. For transactions using contracts such as murabahah, mudharabah, musyarakah, or ijarah, the records should identify the contract, parties, object, price or capital contribution, agreed margin or profit-sharing ratio, payment schedule, and outstanding obligations as relevant. Excel itself does not certify sharia compliance; that assessment depends on the validity of the contract and the actual conduct of the parties. The article concludes that Excel is a practical initial tool for MSMEs when supported by clear procedures, adequate user knowledge, internal checks, and accounting treatment appropriate to the transaction and

latest.title: Pengaruh Economic Value Added, Earning Per Share, dan Ukuran Perusahaan Terhadap Kelayakan Investasi Saham pada Perusahaan Sektor Telekomunikasi yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of Economic Value Added (EVA), Earnings Per Share (EPS), and firm size on stock investment feasibility in telecommunications companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2022–2025. Stock investment feasibility is proxied by the Price Earnings Ratio (PER). This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from quarterly financial statements. The population consists of 17 telecommunications companies, from which 11 companies were selected through purposive sampling based on the availability of complete quarterly financial statements. The final dataset comprises 176 observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-tests, and an F-test with IBM SPSS Statistics version 25. The results show that EVA, EPS, and firm size each have a positive and statistically significant effect on PER. Simultaneously, the three independent variables have a significant effect on PER. The coefficient of determination indicates that approximately 34.3% of the variation in PER is explained by EVA, EPS, and firm size, while the remaining variation is explained by other factors outside the research model. These findings suggest that investors may consider value creation, earnings per share, and company scale as part of fundamental analysis when assessing telecommunications stocks.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on organizational performance: The mediating role of employee productivity
hot.venue: Journal of Open Innovation Technology Market and Complexity
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the workplace is becoming more common, with several research highlighting both its positive and adverse influence on employee productivity (EP) and organizational performance (OP). Furthermore, there is a scarcity of research focused on the mediator role of EP in the nexus between AI and OP. This ambiguity underscores the need for a comprehensive understanding of how AI interacts with EP and OP within specific organizational contexts, such as Ethio Telecom. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI on OP with a mediating role of EP. Quantitative data was collected through an online survey using Kobo Toolbox from 172 purposively selected employees. AI was modeled as third-order formative construct, while EP and OP were first-order reflective constructs. The variables were measured using validated multi-item questionnaires with a 7-point Likert scale. The association between these variables was investigated with PLS-SEM in SMART PLS 4.1.03. The results showed that there were positive and significant relationships between AI and EP, AI and OP, EP and OP, and AI on OP through EP. Furthermore, EP served as a partial mediator between OP and AI. These findings are consistent with previous studies and theories, such as the resource-based view and human capital theories. The results suggest that organizations can dramatically improve performance in the digital age by implementing AI and creating a work environment that encourages productivity.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings.
