hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Global supply chains : why they emerged, why they matter, and where they are going
hot.venue: Graduate Institute Geneva Institutional Repository (Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies)
hot.abstract: Global supply chains have transformed the world. They revolutionised development options facing poor nations – now they can join supply chains rather than having to invest decades in building their own. Offshoring of labour-intensive manufacturing stages and the attendant international mobility of technology launched era-defining growth in emerging markets – a change that fosters and is fostered by domestic policy reform. Historic income gaps are narrowing as the North de-industrialises and the South industrialises -- a reversal-of-fortunes that constitutes perhaps the most momentous global economic change in the last 100 years. Global supply chains, however, are themselves rapidly evolving. The change is in part due to their own impact (income and wage convergence) and in part due to rapid technological innovations in communication technology, computer integrated manufacturing, 3D printing, etc. This paper looks at why global supply chains (GSCs) matter, the economics of their unbundling, and their implications for policy. It finishes with a discussion of factors affecting the future of global supply chains. The paper begins by putting global supply chains into historical perspective.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In the modern business environment, green or sustainable claims mushroom, with companies striving to improve their green practices for climate change and sustainability. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure, which may create opportunities to exploit sustainable efforts to their advantage. Many companies assert environmental-friendly measures to mask their true activities, the phenomenon, known as greenwashing, fuels public scepticism about the sincerity of their green message. This study employs an event study methodology to explore how the stock market values greenwashing announcements through 121 worldwide greenwashing announcements since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal that a modest negative association between greenwashing announcements and stock market reactions. Notably, the market reaction to greenwashing announcements is more negative for firms with greater environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance than for weak ESG performance. The study further finds that there are more negative reactions to announcements providing solid evidence of greenwashing. The companies operating in the manufacturing industry suffer more market value losses than those operating in the service industry. Compared with other stock markets, the Asia-Pacific market experiences negative reactions to greenwashing. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainable practices by offering empirical insights within a global context.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Cross-lagged panel networks
hot.abstract: Network theory and accompanying methodology are becoming increasingly popular as an alternative to latent variable models for representing and, ultimately, understanding psychological constructs. The core feature of network models is that observed variables (e.g., symptoms of depression) directly influence one another over time (e.g., low mood --> concentration problems), resulting in an interconnected dynamical system. The dynamics of such a system might result in certain states (e.g., a depressive episode). Network modeling has been applied to cross-sectional data and intensive longitudinal designs (e.g., data collected using an Experience Sampling Method). In this paper, we present a cross-lagged panel network model to reveal item-level longitudinal effects that occur within and across constructs that are measured at a small set of measurement occasions. The proposed model uses a combination of regularized regression estimation and structural equation modeling to estimate auto-regressive and cross-lagged pathways that characterize the effects of observed components of psychological constructs on each other over time. We demonstrate the application of this model to longitudinal data on students' commitment to school and self-esteem.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: AI capability and green innovation impact on sustainable performance: Moderating role of big data and knowledge management
The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Guidelines for Theory Selection: The IMPACT Framework
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Though the role of adopting an appropriate theory in shaping the publishability and impact of research has long been recognized, psychology and marketing researchers lack specific guidance on how to choose a theory to frame their work. Addressing this gap in the literature, this article proposes a set of guidelines for the selection of relevant macro‐foundational theory to guide research projects addressing specific meso‐ or micro‐foundational theoretical entities (e.g., constructs or individual decision‐making) for research impact. Specifically, we develop a set of six guidelines to select an appropriate macro‐foundational theory for research impact, including Interestingness , Matching , Parsimony , Applicability , Conceptual rigor , and Testability (collectively abbreviated as the “IMPACT” guidelines). We next depict the proposed guidelines in an organizing framework that specifies Matching , the theoretical co ‐infusion of the studied micro‐ or meso‐foundational theoretical entity and the chosen macro‐foundational theory, as the central action item for researchers to shape the impact of their work. Researchers are then advised to use the five remaining guidelines to assess the quality of their proposed Matching for research impact. We conclude by discussing pertinent implications that arise from our analyses (e.g., to ensure Interestingness , we recommend researchers to select a macro‐foundational theory that refutes (vs. affirms) prior findings).

hot.title: Sustainability or Greenwashing: Evidence from the Asset Market for Industrial Pollution
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT We study the asset market for pollutive plants. Firms divest pollutive plants in response to environmental pressures. Buyers are firms facing weaker environmental pressures that have supply chain relationships or joint ventures with the sellers. While pollution levels do not decline following divestitures, sellers highlight their sustainable policies in subsequent conference calls, earn higher returns as they sell more pollutive plants, and benefit from higher Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings and lower compliance costs. Overall, the asset market allows firms to redraw their boundaries in a manner perceived as environmentally friendly without real consequences for pollution but with substantial gains from trade.

latest.title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
latest.abstract: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

latest.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
latest.abstract: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. Findings indicate that AVI outbreaks have been characterized by fear, disgust, and avoidance of poultry products. Many of the other psychological phenomena observed in AVI outbreaks have been documented in past pandemics and other infectious outbreaks: Blame and anger, disease-related avoidance and stigmatization, xenophobia, conspiracy theories, panic buying, and personal stockpiling have all arisen in response to AVI outbreaks. These psychological phenomena may persist and intensify if AVI outbreaks evolve into a pandemic. The lessons learned from COVID-19 can be used to prepare for a possible AVI pandemic. However, additional measures may be needed. Fear, disgust, and avoidance of specific foods would likely distinguish an AVI pandemic from COVID-19. The threat of infected food triggers disgust, and so food-related disgust would likely be a prominent emotional reaction during an AVI pandemic. Public messaging from health authorities and others has the potential to either ease or exacerbate public concerns about food safety, depending on how the messages are crafted.

latest.title: Genuine association or spurious responding? Experimental evidence on the correlation between cryptocurrency trading and problem gambling severity index scores
latest.abstract: Abstract Background and aims Cryptocurrency trading has become a popular activity worldwide, which has been correlated with harmful gambling as measured by the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI). However, in addition to being non-causal, these correlations may partly or in whole follow from methodological weaknesses, such as failing to screen out non-gamblers, or failing to instruct participants to not consider cryptocurrency trading a form of gambling. Methods In a large-scale pre-registered 2 × 2 online experiment (N = 4,781), we hypothesised that if observed correlations were driven by spurious responding, they would be credibly weakened by screening out non-gamblers (compared to no screening), and by instructing participants to not consider cryptocurrency trading as a form of gambling (compared to no-instruction). Cryptocurrency trading engagement was assessed via self-reported trading frequency, price monitoring frequency, and number of coins owned over the past year. Results While gambling screening lowered reported PGSI scores, trading frequency remained positively associated with the PGSI across all conditions ( β = 0.008, 95% HPDI [0.007, 0.010]), with no credible evidence that screening or instruction moderated the association. Exploratory analyses showed similar patterns for price monitoring frequency and the number of coins owned. A combined model showed that trading frequency explained the most variance in the PGSI outcomes. Conclusions These findings provide further evidence of a genuine correlation between cryptocurrency trading and harmful gambling, and may inform future research and policy discussions regarding how gambling-related consumer protections could be relevant to cryptocurrencies.

latest.title: Market Structure and Export Competitiveness in the Global Mango Trade: An HHI, CMS and RSCA Approach (2006–2024)
latest.abstract: Abstract The present study investigates the competitiveness of the global fresh mango market from 2006 to 2024. HHI scores between 673.75 and 848.18 indicate a high level of competition and market diversification, rather than a monopoly. The CMS analysis reveals that Thailand recorded a positive value of 578,997 tons, while India recorded a negative value of -661,383 tons. In 2024, Peru and Pakistan had scores between 0.86 and 0.95, while India's score decreased sharply from 0.90 in 2006 to 0.35 in 2024. The results of the econometric models for 16 countries show that Agricultural Productivity positively affects overall market competitiveness (β = 0.351; p < 0.001), while Import Unit value Index negatively affects overall market competitiveness (β = -0.353; p < 0.001). A hybrid strategy, however, was effective in boosting competitiveness in Spain even as import prices rose (β = 0.525; p = 0.038), as indicated by country-specific models. The results confirm that quality leadership, value-added products, and market diversification are not only important for achieving economies of scale and bulk production, but also for sustaining a competitive advantage.

latest.title: VAT Treatment of Core Crypto Transactions in the System of EU VAT and Beyond
latest.abstract: Transactions in virtual crypto assets challenge VAT systems that were designed for conventional business models. With a particular focus on the common system of EU VAT, this article examines the treatment of core crypto transactions involving payment tokens, NFTs and utility tokens. It argues that crypto assets cannot be classified generically for VAT purposes. Instead, their treatment depends on the technological design of the relevant blockchain mechanism and the economic function of the token. The analysis addresses VAT issues related to mining and staking, trading in primary and secondary markets, the use of tokens, and the services provided by portal and interface operators. It includes an assessment of deemed supplier regimes for crypto platforms, margin schemes, and a special regime for vouchers from a VAT law and policy perspective. The article further shows that crypto pseudonymity creates particular difficulties for applying the destination principle, determining the taxable amount, and enforcing VAT liabilities, and presents possible solutions. The article thereby identifies the key issues that need to be addressed by any VAT/GST system to ensure adequate, neutral and efficient taxation of crypto assets.

latest.title: Improving the Competitiveness Management Mechanism of Service Enterprises
latest.venue: Academic Journal of Digital Economics and Stability
latest.abstract: This article analyzes issues related to improving the mechanism for managing the competitiveness of service enterprises. The role of the service sector in the national economy, its share in the gross domestic product, and its importance in economic development are scientifically examined. In addition, the factors influencing the increase of competitiveness of service enterprises, the ways of effectively organizing management mechanisms, and the development trends of the service market in modern economic conditions are considered.

latest.title: Organizational and Economic Aspects of Increasing The Competitiveness of Service Enterprises Mechanisms
latest.venue: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
latest.abstract: The competitive advantage of service enterprises is vital for their success in modern market economies. Effective management of competitiveness through organizational and economic mechanisms is essential in maintaining long-term viability in a rapidly evolving market. This is particularly relevant in Uzbekistan's service sector, where globalization and technological advancements have intensified competition. Service enterprises must leverage strategic management, innovation, and resource optimization to gain and sustain competitive advantages. Although various theories exist on competitive advantage, including Porter's framework and the resource-based approach, a detailed analysis of integrated organizational, economic, and marketing mechanisms tailored to the service industry remains underexplored. This study aims to identify and evaluate the key strategies for enhancing the competitiveness of service enterprises in Uzbekistan. It explores how competitive advantages are formed through cost leadership, differentiation, and specialization strategies, focusing on the service sector's unique characteristics. The research highlights that integrating organizational, economic, and innovative mechanisms leads to sustainable competitive advantage. Key strategies such as cost optimization, service differentiation, and digital transformation were identified as critical factors in strengthening competitiveness. This study offers a comprehensive approach that incorporates modern management theories with industry-specific factors to develop effective competitive strategies for service enterprises. The findings suggest practical recommendations for service enterprises, including the adoption of flexible pricing systems, digital service enhancements, and workforce training. Further re

latest.title: From Online Engagement to Heritage Visits: Mapping Consumer Pathways in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tourism
latest.abstract: This study investigates how heritage sites in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) are portrayed through digital storytelling across various online platforms and how these narratives influence the cyber-customer path in tourism decision-making. Using qualitative content analysis, the research examines 40 digital media artifacts including Instagram posts, YouTube travel vlogs, tourism blogs, and official promotional websites to identify how different stages of the cyber-customer journey (awareness, interest, evaluation, decision, and advocacy) are represented in the content. The study discloses that platforms like Instagram and YouTube use highly visual and emotional storytelling to create initial awareness and interest, while blogs and official websites provide evaluative content that supports travel decisions. Key stakeholders in these narratives include influencers, government tourism bodies, and travel communities. The research highlights digital media’s significant role in shaping heritage perceptions, encouraging responsible tourism, and connecting audiences to cultural narratives through engaging formats. The findings contribute to media studies and heritage tourism by providing a model for analysing the intersection of storytelling, tourism behaviour, and digital media strategy.

latest.title: Влияние социальных сетей на международный маркетинг
latest.abstract: В статье исследуется трансформация инструментария международного маркетинга под влиянием глобальных социальных платформ. Рассмотрены ключевые барьеры адаптации маркетинговых стратегий при выходе брендов на зарубежные рынки, включая кросс-культурные различия, правовые ограничения и региональную специфику алгоритмов дистрибуции контента. На основе анализа метрик вовлеченности, стоимости привлечения клиента и возврата инвестиций определена эффективная структура распределения ресурсов между глобальными и локальными каналами коммуникации. Выявлена зависимость показателей конверсии от степени интеграции микроинфлюенсеров в локальные маркетинговые кампании.

latest.title: Strategic trajectories of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail: a matrix approach
latest.abstract: The article develops a matrix-based model for selecting strategic trajectories of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail aimed at identifying mismatches between internal digital readiness and the actual level of technology adoption. The proposed approach combines two interrelated strategic dimensions: digital readiness, reflecting management commitment, digital potential, organizational culture, and digital strategy, and technology adoption, characterizing the extent to which digital solutions are embedded in customer-facing, operational, analytical, and logistics processes. An additional readiness-adoption gap is introduced to assess the degree to which accumulated internal digital capabilities are converted into implemented technological solutions. The research is based on system, comparative, structural-logical, and analytical approaches, as well as methods of grouping, synthesis, scientific generalization, and sample-relative positioning. The results indicate that a high level of internal digital capability does not necessarily correspond to an equally intensive level of technology adoption, while similar technological configurations may require different managerial responses depending on the internal capability structure of the retailer. The relationship between digital readiness and technology adoption is therefore interpreted not as a static maturity characteristic but as a dynamic strategic configuration reflecting the balance between organizational potential and technological implementation. To translate diagnostic results into managerial decisions, a matrix of four strategic trajectories is proposed: scaling and differentiation, mobilization of latent capability, consolidation and balancing of digital capabilities, and foundation building. Each traject

latest.title: Influence of AI personalization on consumer loyalty in the restaurant business: balance between efficiency and ethics
latest.abstract: The article examines the influence of artificial intelligence-based personalization on the formation of consumer loyalty in the restaurant business. Current trends in the implementation of AI tools, including recommendation systems, dynamic pricing, and loyalty programs, as well as their impact on customer experience, are analyzed. Based on an analysis of empirical data and scholarly publications, key factors determining the effectiveness of AI personalization are identified: relevance of offers, transparency of data use, and preservation of «human» contact. Particular attention is paid to ethical aspects - issues of privacy, risks of dehumanization of service, and manipulative influence on consumer choice. A model for balanced implementation of AI personalization is proposed, taking into account both economic efficiency and ethical constraints. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of applying the proposed recommendations in forming digital transformation strategies for restaurant enterprises.

latest.title: Adaptive omnichannel brand management architecture for light industry enterprises: from brand identity to performance control
latest.abstract: The article substantiates an integrated approach to brand management in light industry enterprises under conditions of digitalization, changing consumer behavior, and increasing fragmentation of interaction channels. Brand management is interpreted as an organizational and functional subsystem that ensures the alignment of strategic positioning, brand identity, communications, digital and physical touchpoints, and analytical control. A three-layer omnichannel brand-management architecture is proposed, comprising the strategic and identity core, the omnichannel interaction layer, and the performance-control layer. The functional content of the system is structured around four interrelated blocks: strategic planning, design, communications, and analytics. Particular attention is paid to the coordination of websites and mobile interfaces, marketplaces, social media, and physical retail within a unified customer journey. The performance-control layer links consumer response, conversion, loyalty, channel efficiency, and economic results, thereby closing the management loop. A recurrent adaptive management cycle is proposed, including diagnosis, identification of structural imbalance, selection of managerial intervention, implementation, measurement, and adjustment. The proposed approach makes it possible to identify structural bottlenecks in brand management and to select differentiated managerial actions aimed at strengthening brand coherence, continuity of customer experience, and market effectiveness.

latest.title: Промышленный туризм: от экскурсии на производство к политике открытости предприятия
latest.abstract: Прослежена эволюция промышленного туризма как практики и научного понятия – от эпизодических визитов на мануфактуры до управляемой открытости предприятия. Использованы историко-генетический метод и сравнение трактовок. Выделены пять этапов развития практики, различающихся задачей, которую решает предприятие, и пять этапов эволюции научных трактовок. Показано, что российская практика перешла к программно-стратегическому этапу, миновав зрелую брендово-сервисную стадию, а в научных трактовках позиция самого предприятия остается наименее разработанной. Обоснован переход к формирующемуся шестому этапу – политике открытости предприятия, в которой промышленный туризм становится одним из инструментов регламентированного доступа заинтересованных сторон к производству, компетенциям и управленческим практикам.

latest.title: Integrated diagnostics of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail
latest.abstract: The article develops an integrated diagnostic model of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail aimed at identifying imbalances between technological development, organizational capabilities, and market outcomes. The proposed approach combines four interrelated diagnostic contours: external digital opportunities, actual technology adoption, internal digital readiness, and customer and market response. The research is based on system, process, comparative, and structural-logical approaches, as well as analysis, synthesis, classification, and scientific generalization. The empirical illustration of the model uses publicly available corporate data for 2025-2026 covering ten Russian FMCG retail chains. Digital readiness is assessed through four components: management commitment, digital potential, digital culture, and digital strategy. The results indicate that relatively balanced average levels of digital readiness coexist with noticeable firm-level differences in their internal configuration. Digital culture demonstrates the highest average value (0.885), whereas digital strategy has the lowest (0.840), suggesting that the development of technological and organizational capabilities may outpace their integration into a coherent long-term transformation agenda. To translate diagnostic results into managerial decisions, a matrix linking specific diagnostic signals with corresponding management responses is proposed. The developed framework supports the identification of capability bottlenecks, underused technologies, customer-journey friction, and inconsistencies between digital readiness and actual technology adoption. Its practical application can facilitate the prioritization of digital initiatives, continuous monitoring, strategic adjustment, control, and recurren

latest.title: Pemanfaatan Microsoft Excel Dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) Perspektif Hukum Ekonomi Syariah
latest.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need orderly financial records to monitor business activities, assess performance, and make responsible economic decisions. For Muslim-owned or sharia-oriented MSMEs, financial administration also has a normative dimension: transactions should be recorded transparently, agreements should be clear, and business practices should avoid riba, gharar, and maysir. This article examines the use of Microsoft Excel in MSME financial management from the perspective of Islamic economic law. It applies a descriptive qualitative literature-review method combined with a normative-conceptual analysis of sharia business principles, relevant regulations, and studies on spreadsheet-based accounting and sharia-oriented MSMEs. The literature indicates that Excel can assist transaction recording, cash-flow monitoring, cost calculation, inventory control, and preparation of financial summaries. From an Islamic economic law perspective, these functions may support the principles of amanah, shiddiq, ‘adl, transparency, and protection of wealth (hifz al-mal), provided that the workbook records the substance of transactions accurately. For transactions using contracts such as murabahah, mudharabah, musyarakah, or ijarah, the records should identify the contract, parties, object, price or capital contribution, agreed margin or profit-sharing ratio, payment schedule, and outstanding obligations as relevant. Excel itself does not certify sharia compliance; that assessment depends on the validity of the contract and the actual conduct of the parties. The article concludes that Excel is a practical initial tool for MSMEs when supported by clear procedures, adequate user knowledge, internal checks, and accounting treatment appropriate to the transaction and

latest.title: Design And Development Of A Web-Based Digital Credit Service And Qris Transaction System
latest.abstract: The rapid development of financial technology (fintech) has accelerated the adoption of digital payment and digital credit services. However, most digital credit services still rely on cash disbursement mechanisms, making it difficult to control the utilization of borrowed funds. This study aims to develop PayQRIS, a web-based Buy Now, Pay Later (PayLater) service integrated with QRIS payments that enables cashless transactions using credit limits without direct cash disbursement. The system was developed using the Prototyping model and evaluated through black-box testing and the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results show that PayQRIS successfully integrates PayLater services with QRIS payments into a single platform featuring credit limit determination, installment and bill management, bill extension, and secure transaction authentication. Functional testing confirmed that all system features operated according to the specified requirements, while the usability evaluation produced a SUS score of 83.25, indicating a high level of usability and user acceptance. Therefore, PayQRIS provides a web-based PayLater solution that supports QRIS payments through a more controlled digital credit mechanism.

latest.title: Analisis Pemanfaatan Aplikasi Fintech Terhadap Inklusi Keuangan Masyarakat: Suatu Kajian Pustaka
latest.abstract: Financial technology (fintech) applications are changing how people access payments, savings, credit, investment, and other financial services. Digital services may reduce distance and cost barriers and reach groups underserved by formal institutions. However, owning a smartphone or digital account does not automatically produce meaningful inclusion if users cannot understand fees, use services safely, or access products suited to their needs. This article analyzes how fintech application use relates to financial inclusion by reviewing mechanisms, benefits, disparities, risks, and policy prerequisites. The narrative literature review covers academic publications, international institutional reports, official Indonesian survey data, regulatory documentation, and consumer-protection sources. The literature indicates a multidimensional relationship: digital payments may serve as an entry point to formal transactions; digital credit may expand financing access while also increasing over-indebtedness risk; and digital savings, microinsurance, and investment require adequate product understanding and safeguards. Indonesia’s 2024 National Survey on Financial Literacy and Inclusion reported a 75.02% financial inclusion index, but this aggregate figure does not isolate the effect of fintech applications. Geography, gender, age, literacy, connectivity, and service quality shape who benefits. Fintech is therefore an enabling channel rather than a substitute for infrastructure, consumer protection, literacy, and sound governance. Impact assessment should distinguish access, active use, quality, affordability, and user welfare.

latest.title: Constrained risk rationalization: how economically vulnerable consumers justify counterfeit purchases in Colombia’s informal markets
latest.abstract: Purpose This study explores how economically constrained mothers rationalize risky purchases of counterfeit household goods in informal markets, extending attention beyond luxury counterfeits and treating caregiving responsibility as a central analytic concern. Design/methodology/approach Using grounded theory, the study analyzes 45 intercept interviews with low-income mothers shopping in two San Andresito markets in Bogotá, Colombia. Analysis used open coding, constant comparison and selective coding, with saturation tracked through a code-emergence log. Findings Mothers rationalize counterfeit purchases through Constrained Risk Rationalization (CRR): economic necessity, social normalization, trust-based mitigation and psychological trade-offs. Together, these mechanisms may help make counterfeit buying a practical, morally defensible response to household need. Research limitations/implications This first-stage qualitative study is bounded to brief interviews with one participant group in one market system. Future research should test CRR through ethnographic and mixed-method designs. Practical implications Risk warnings may be less effective when consumers already know the risks but perceive few alternatives. Responses may be more effective if they focus on affordability, community trust and safer local options. Social implications Counterfeit purchasing in informal markets is tied to poverty, exclusion and provisioning pressures; reducing it may require addressing these conditions, not enforcement or deterrence alone. Originality/value The paper extends counterfeit consumption research beyond luxury goods, offering a process-based account of how necessity, norms, trust and coping may operate together, and brings gendered caregiving responsibility into counterfeit co

latest.title: Validity of Actigraphy and Sleep Diary Compared With Home Polysomnography in Patients With Sleep Apnea and Insomnia Symptoms
latest.abstract: Objective To evaluate the validity of actigraphy and sleep diaries against home polysomnography (PSG) and to determine whether their performance differs according to sleep apnea and insomnia.Methods Participants underwent one-night home PSG with actigraphy and next-morning sleep diary completion. Parameters included total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency (SE), sleep latency (SL), and wake after sleep onset (WASO). The apnea subgroup was defined as apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15, and the insomnia symptoms subgroup as Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index >5 and AHI <15. Mean differences, correlations, correlation comparisons, and agreement with PSG were evaluated.Results A total of 63 adults (mean age 49.7±14.0 years; 27 male) were included. Overall, actigraphy overestimated TST and SE and underestimated SL, whereas sleep diaries overestimated SL. Both tools were significantly correlated with PSG across all parameters, with sleep diaries showing a stronger correlation with PSG for SL (r=0.817 vs. 0.438, p<0.001). In both the apnea and insomnia symptoms subgroups, actigraphy was significantly correlated with PSG only for TST (ρ=0.594 and 0.462). In contrast, sleep diaries were significantly correlated with PSG for all parameters in the insomnia symptoms subgroup (ρ=0.668–0.781), but only for WASO in the apnea subgroup (ρ=0.440).Conclusion Both actigraphy and sleep diaries showed validity relative to PSG, but their clinical use should be tailored to the underlying sleep disorder. Sleep diaries may be particularly informative in insomnia, whereas actigraphy may be relatively more useful in sleep apnea.

latest.title: How Does Cognitive Dissonance Explain Why Consumers Justify Expensive Purchases After the Fact (Post-Purchase Rationalization), And What Does This Mean for Return-Policy Design?
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This paper explores the cognitive dissonance theory developed by Leon Festinger (Festinger, 1957) as an answer to explain why consumers in their normal practices justify their high-cost purchases after they make them. This is often referred to as post-purchase rationalization and/or "buyer's remorse management". Based on the social-psychological literature on dissonance reduction, the consumer-behaviour research on post-purchase evaluation (Oliver, 1980; Sweeney, Hausknecht, & Soutar, 2000), and the current literature on retail returns (National Retail Federation & Happy Returns, 2024, 2025), the paper proposes a framework that integrates purchase involvement, decision irreversibility, and self-concept threat with the intensity of post-purchase dissonance and the rationalization strategies consumers use to manage it. The paper then moves on to the implications of this psychology for the firm, that is, the design of return policies. The ease at which a consumer can reverse a purchase decision has a direct effect on the psychological dynamics of dissonance, with lenient return policies making customers more likely to convert to a purchase and causing a window where dissonance can arise as an actual return. The paper utilizes data from the National Retail Federation, Janakiraman, Syrdal, and Freling (2016) meta-analysis of the U.S. retail return literature, and other secondary sources to illustrate that there were an estimated $890 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2024 (16.9% of sales), a slight decrease to estimated $849.9 billion worth of U.S. retail returns in 2025 (15.8%), and leniency dimensions (e.g. monetary, temporal, effort, scope and exchange) have an asymmetric influence on purchase and return behaviour. The paper ends with a section on policy design that

latest.title: Analisis Penerapan Meta Ads dalam Meningkatkan Brand Awareness Digital pada Sektor Konstruksi
latest.abstract: Digital branding menjadi strategi penting bagi perusahaan konstruksi untuk membangun citra perusahaan yang profesional dan terpercaya. Penelitian ini menganalisis pengembangan digital branding melalui media sosial dan Meta Ads pada PT Hotmix Karya Indonesia, perusahaan produksi aspal panas dan infrastruktur jalan. Penelitian menggunakan metode deskriptif kualitatif yang didukung data kuantitatif performa iklan, dengan data dikumpulkan melalui observasi lapangan, wawancara, dan dokumentasi selama empat bulan. Hasil menunjukkan Instagram digunakan sebagai platform utama untuk konten edukasi, dokumentasi, dan promosi yang memperkuat citra profesional perusahaan. Kampanye Meta Ads menjangkau 1.088 orang dengan 1.461 impresi dan 63 interaksi bersih, menghasilkan click-through rate 3,29% dan engagement rate 5,79%, keduanya di atas benchmark industri secara umum. Efektivitas masih terkendala keterbatasan sumber daya manusia, pengelolaan konten yang belum konsisten, dan anggaran. Analisis fishbone mengidentifikasi faktor man, method, dan material sebagai penyebab utama, yang menjadi dasar usulan perbaikan. Penelitian menyimpulkan bahwa Meta Ads menunjukkan indikasi positif terhadap peningkatan eksposur dan brand awareness digital, berdasarkan data jangkauan dan impresi, bukan pengukuran langsung, sehingga perlu diperkuat dengan sumber daya memadai, pengelolaan konten terstruktur, dan penelitian lanjutan.

latest.title: An exploratory predictive model of sustainable consumption behaviour in FMCG packaging markets
latest.abstract: This study examines how consumers' overall evaluation of sustainably packaged fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) relates to their purchasing behaviour. Survey data were collected from 206 consumers across eleven Indian cities using a structured questionnaire covering four conceptually distinct facets of this evaluation: perceptions of sustainable packaging, product experience, post-purchase satisfaction, and loyalty-related attitudes, measured through 23 Likert-scale items. Exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, and discriminant-validity testing (heterotrait-monotrait ratios) showed that these four facets could not be empirically distinguished from one another in this sample. The items were therefore combined into a single sustainable consumption evaluation (SCE) Index of 21 items, after excluding weakly-loading item (α = .89; KMO = .91). Next, the SCE Index is tested as a predictor of three outcomes measured independently of the index itself: purchase frequency, the share of a respondent's FMCG purchases that are sustainably packaged and stated preference for sustainable over regular packaging. The index significantly predicted all three outcomes (standardised β = .21 and .30 for the two continuous outcomes; odds ratio 3.31 for preference; all p < .01). These findings suggest that, among the consumers sampled, sustainable-packaging perception, product experience, and post-purchase satisfaction function as a single, undifferentiated evaluative judgement rather than as separable psychological constructs, and that this judgement meaningfully predicts sustainable purchasing behaviour and preference.

latest.title: FORMATION OF A BUSINESS MODEL FOR THE COMMERCIALIZATION OF ADAPTIVE SPATIAL LIGHTING TECHNOLOGY
latest.abstract: The article substantiates a business model for the commercialization of adaptive spatial lighting technology based on the transformation of its functional and technological characteristics into consumer and market value. The study identifies the key technological features that determine the commercialization potential of the proposed solution, including a three-dimensional LED structure, the integration of information-visual and lighting-spectral channels, adaptive control, sensor-based interaction, and compatibility with the user’s digital environment. Functional, adaptive-personalized, and integrative components of the value proposition are distinguished. It is shown that the commercialization potential of the technology is formed not by individual technical parameters but by their interconnected combination, which expands product functionality and creates opportunities for market differentiation. The main components of the business model are defined as the technological core, value proposition, target market, configuration of value creation and delivery, and the economic result of commercialization. The proposed model reflects the sequence of transformation of technological capabilities into market-relevant value and considers the interdependence between product functionality, customer needs, target-market parameters, resources, participants in value creation, and methods of delivering value to the market. The model also incorporates the influence of market, technological, competitive, institutional and regulatory factors, as well as intellectual property protection. Feedback links between commercialization outcomes, the target market, the value proposition, and the technological core are included, which reflects the adaptive nature of the proposed business model. Th

latest.title: Market Competition, Pricing Strategy, and Firm Performance: An Economic Perspective
latest.venue: Empirical Studies in Econimics and Finance
latest.abstract: Market competition plays an important role in shaping firms’ pricing decisions and overall performance. This study examines the relationship between market competition, pricing strategy, and firm performance from an economic perspective. Drawing on theories of market structure, price elasticity of demand, and profit maximization, the study analyzes how different competitive conditions influence firms’ pricing behavior. It examines several major pricing approaches, including costbased pricing, competition-based pricing, value-based pricing, and dynamic pricing, and considers their implications for profitability, market share, and long-term competitive performance. The analysis further identifies product differentiation, consumer price sensitivity, market concentration, firm characteristics, and digital technologies as important factors affecting the relationship between competition, pricing, and performance. The findings suggest that pricing strategy does not have a uniform effect on firm performance. Lower prices may stimulate demand and market share but can reduce profit margins, whereas higher prices may improve margins while negatively affecting demand when consumers are price sensitive. Therefore, firms need to align pricing decisions with market structure, consumer demand, competitive conditions, and long-term strategic objectives. The study highlights the importance of integrating economic principles with strategic pricing decisions in increasingly competitive and technology-driven markets.

latest.title: Peran Digital Marketing dan Interactivity dalam Brand Image dan Minat Beli Ulang Produk Geoff Max
latest.abstract: Previous research findings on the effects of digital marketing and interactivity on brand image and repurchase intention remain mixed, particularly regarding direct effects and the mediating role of brand image. This study aimed to analyze the effects of digital marketing and interactivity on brand image and repurchase intention for Geoff Max products, while also testing the role of brand image as a mediating variable. The study employed a quantitative approach with a survey design involving 100 Geoff Max consumers as respondents. Data were collected through a questionnaire and analyzed using the SEM-PLS method. The results showed that digital marketing had a positive and significant effect on brand image, whereas interactivity did not show a significant effect. Brand image had a significant effect on repurchase intention, while digital marketing and interactivity did not show significant direct effects on repurchase intention. Mediation testing also provided no evidence that brand image mediated the relationships of either digital marketing or interactivity with repurchase intention. These findings clarify the distinction between direct effects among variables and the mediating role of brand image in the context of Geoff Max consumers. This study concludes that digital marketing plays a role in shaping brand image and that brand image is associated with repurchase intention, although the mediation relationships tested were not confirmed. In practical terms, the findings inform companies’ considerations when optimizing digital marketing and strengthening brand image through consistent marketing communication and the articulation of product value relevant to consumer needs.

latest.title: Omnichannel integration in fashion retail: privacy barriers to customer retention
latest.venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose Focusing on fashion retail, this study investigates how customer-perceived channel integration (CPCI) influences privacy concerns (PC) and customer retention (CR), specifically testing whether PC mediates the link between integration and retention. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the “Stimulus–Organism–Response” model and privacy calculus theory, this study explores omnichannel retail consumer behaviour (ORCB). Data were collected via in-person surveys from 600 Generation Y customers in Ankara. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling was employed to examine the direct and indirect pathways within the model. Findings The results indicate that retail CPCI is positively associated with CR and negatively associated with PC. PC partially mediates the CPCI–CR relationship, indicating that integrated omnichannel experiences relate to retention both directly and indirectly through lower privacy-related anxieties. Research limitations/implications Generalisability is bounded by the focus on a single metropolitan area. Future research should incorporate diverse demographic cohorts and cross-cultural settings to extend these findings. Practical implications Fashion retailers should transition towards “privacy-by-design” frameworks. By implementing transparent consent mechanisms and consistent service delivery, retailers can alleviate PC and strengthen long-term customer relationships. Originality/value This study shows that PC operate as a negative organism-level mediator: integration quality strengthens retention partly by easing privacy concerns, a channel carrying about a third of the total effect that positive-state-only models overlook, and one sharpened by fashion's identity-expressive data exposure.

latest.title: From Default Risk to Priced Intervention: A Cost-Benefit Approach to Credit Card Risk Management
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Credit card default prediction is a mature application of machine learning in consumer finance, yet published studies typically stop at discrimination metrics without connecting a model’s output to the economics of a specific intervention a bank could actually deploy. This paper builds an interpretable default-risk model using the public UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (Yeh and Lien, 2009) and couples it to a cost-benefit framework built from cited, real-world figures. A logistic regression baseline achieves test ROC-AUC of 0.741, and a random forest comparison model achieves 0.780, on a cohort of 30,000 Taiwanese credit card clients with a 22.12% next-month default rate. Rather than a single flat dollar loss, this paper estimates avoided loss per client from the client’s own most recent bill amount multiplied by a published average loss-given-default rate for credit cards (61.54%; Bellotti & Crook, 2012). Against this, two realistic intervention channels are costed: an SMS reminder ($0.03) and a live-agent call ($2.70, reused from a companion study), with effectiveness drawn from a randomized field experiment on credit card debt repayment (a 4.4-percentage-point reduction in delinquency; Bursztyn, Fiorin, Gottlieb, & Kanz, 2019). Under these figures, the break-even cost per intervention for untargeted, blanket outreach is $457.45, far above both realistic channel costs, so model-based targeting adds negligible net value over contacting every client at either cost. This paper argues the finding is not a property of the models but of the ratio between typical credit card exposure sizes and low-cost communication channels, and discusses what would need to change for precision targeting to matter in this setting.

latest.title: Para-authenticity, ontological flexibility, and ontological detachment: how creatives construct and manage virtual endorsers
latest.abstract: Research on virtual endorsers has largely focused on consumers, leaving the creative strategies behind their development underexplored. This study examines how creatives construct and manage the authenticity of virtual influencers and brand ambassadors while navigating an evolving ethical landscape. Based on in-depth interviews with eleven practitioners, our findings suggest they deliberately construct virtual personas plausibly situated in recognizable social and material worlds despite their artificiality. To manage the tension between brand control and perceived relatability, practitioners integrate imperfections and contextual cues to evoke para-authenticity – a strategic illusion of plausibility. We also explore the business case for virtual endorsers and how practitioners navigate ethical complexities through strategic disclosure, ontological flexibility (the capacity to vary an endorser’s form), and ontological detachment (the ethically ambivalent use of such flexibility to move beyond human embodiment and its associated demographic categories). Overall, this study reframes authenticity as a strategic construction in a synthetic advertising landscape.

Waking Up to the Working Day Ahead: A Diary Study on the Role of Flow in Linking Morning Anticipatory Appraisals to Recovery
latest.abstract: Abstract In this diary study, we investigated how employees’ morning anticipatory appraisals relate to their flow experiences at work and their subsequent recovery after work. Drawing on transactional stress theory, we explored how four types of morning anticipatory appraisal—positive, challenge, threat, and hindrance—predict daily flow at work, and whether flow, in turn, is associated with energy in the evening and affective rumination at bedtime. A total of 102 employees completed three daily surveys across ten consecutive working days. The results from multilevel mediation analysis revealed that morning anticipatory challenge and positive appraisal were positively related to daily flow, while anticipatory threat appraisal was negatively associated with flow. Flow, in turn, predicted lower affective rumination at bedtime and mediated the effects of morning anticipatory appraisals on this outcome. Contrary to expectations, flow was not significantly related to evening energy levels and did not mediate the effects at the within-person level. In conclusion, our results suggest that morning anticipatory appraisals formed before the working day are meaningfully related to employee well-being by shaping the likelihood of experiencing flow at work and the extent of work-related rumination at bedtime. In doing so, this study advances stress and recovery theory by identifying flow as a key mechanism linking early-day cognitive expectations to evening recovery outcomes, and by highlighting the anticipatory phase as a promising target for interventions aimed at improving employees’ day-to-day functioning.

latest.title: Made by humans? Human-AI co-creation, the human-origin premium and brand authenticity in the age of generative AI
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper asks when and why perceived human involvement in AI-assisted brand creation adds relational value, and when co-creation outperforms human-only or AI-only creation. Drawing on research on brand authenticity, human-AI collaboration, creative authorship, effort and presence, signalling and consumer-brand relationships, it develops a dual-pathway framework and seven propositions. The central argument is that consumers judge AI use by inferring who retained consequential judgement over the output, not by asking whether a machine was involved. Distinguishing augmentation from substitution therefore explains why the same level of AI involvement can produce opposite outcomes. A human pathway running through intentionality, effort and presence supports authenticity, while an AI pathway running through competence and consistency supports functional evaluation. Which pathway carries more weight depends on brand type, emotional consequence, transparency and category norms. Because generative assistance makes origin divisible, consumers must allocate credit within a single artefact, and the paper specifies the human-origin premium as a conditional and falsifiable effect of that allocation. It separates what assistance does to the work from what disclosure does to the credit, and distinguishes generic AI labels from role-specific disclosure that reveals consequential human decision rights. For managers, the framework indicates when to preserve and signal human control, when to foreground machine competence and why ceremonial involvement is a liability. The propositions call for experimental and longitudinal testing across categories, cultures and levels of AI involvement.

latest.title: Criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility of enterprises in wartime conditions
latest.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
latest.abstract: The article examines the criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility under the specific conditions of wartime business operations. The study aims to substantiate and systematize criteria and indicators that can comprehensively characterize responsible corporate behavior and reflect changes in the needs and expectations of key stakeholder groups under war-related challenges. The study’s methodological framework draws on analysis and synthesis, systematization and generalization of scientific approaches, the stakeholder approach, and comparative analysis of contemporary research on corporate social responsibility in stable and crisis conditions. The study systematizes six interrelated criteria of corporate social responsibility: social and labor responsibility, economic responsibility, responsibility toward consumers and business partners, ethical and managerial responsibility, environmental responsibility, and social responsibility toward communities and society. The main indicators characterizing each area of responsible corporate behavior are identified. The wartime dimension should not be treated as an isolated area of corporate social responsibility. Instead, it should be considered as a cross-cutting characteristic that changes the content and priority of individual indicators within the established criteria. Wartime-specific manifestations include preserving employment, supporting mobilized employees and their families, ensuring business continuity, adapting business processes to war-related risks, providing humanitarian assistance, supporting local communities, assisting affected populations, and participating in recovery processes. The study’s scientific novelty lies in systematizing CSR criteria by combining universal characteristics of responsibl

latest.title: Modern approaches to managing production and sales activities of enterprises
latest.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
latest.abstract: The article examines modern approaches to managing the production and sales activities of enterprises operating under the difficult conditions of Ukraine’s economic transformation, market globalization, and increased competitive pressure. The author outlines the theoretical foundations of managing production and sales processes, shows their interdependence, and highlights their importance in ensuring enterprise efficiency. The paper focuses on systemic, process, marketing, logistics, and innovation-digital approaches, which, in modern conditions, serve as the conceptual basis for effective management decisions. The paper assesses Ukrainian enterprises’ operational practices. It analyzes the strengths of existing mechanisms, including consumer-oriented focus, the development of new sales channels, and the gradual digitalization of management processes. At the same time, it identifies several problems, including insufficient integration between production and sales subsystems, limited flexibility in management structures, limited use of modern information systems, and a primary focus on short-term financial results. The article supports the feasibility of shifting from fragmented management tools to integrated mechanisms that combine strategic planning, logistics solutions, marketing analytics, and digital technologies. It is shown that integrated management models create opportunities to increase resource efficiency, reduce costs, ensure adaptability, and build long-term competitive advantages. The study proposes directions for improving production and sales management, including using a single information space, increasing client interest, and adapting to changes in the external environment. The practical significance of the results lies in the potential to apply the de

latest.abstract: Finding a reliable streaming service that handles high-stakes sporting fixtures without stuttering can be a real headache for viewers in Australia. SubscribeIP tackles this challenge head-on by deploying dedicated edge servers optimised specifically for local broadband infrastructure, ensuring rock-solid stability even during peak viewing periods. Whether you are settling in for Friday night footy or watching a day-night cricket test, this service offers a polished, dependable alternative to traditional pay-television networks. The platform boasts an extensive catalogue of domestic and international feeds, giving Australian households instant access to major sporting codes including the AFL, NRL, Super Rugby, and global motorsport championships. In addition to high-octane sports, subscribers gain access to all regional free-to-air feeds, metropolitan news broadcasts, and premier entertainment channels from the UK, North America, and New Zealand, all neatly mapped into a coherent electronic programme guide. Setting up SubscribeIP on popular streaming hardware like Apple TV, Amazon Firestick, or Android-powered smart tellies is straightforward thanks to full M3U and Xtream Codes API support. latest.title: Financial Technology and Financial Inclusion: Evidence from East African Community Member Countries
latest.venue: Journal of finance and investment analysis
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of financial technology on financial inclusion in the eight East African Community member countries over 2014–2023, using a balanced panel of 80 country-year observations. Fintech is measured by penetration rate, usage rate and transaction intensity (mobile-money transactions per adult), with GDP per capita, inflation, financial literacy and bank-branch density as controls. Panel unit root and Kao cointegration tests are reported, and random-effects and fixed-effects estimators are compared with the Hausman test (χ²(5) = 4.79, p = 0.441), with two-way fixed effects, first differences and correlated random effects as robustness checks. Penetration rate (β = 4.965, p = 0.002) and transaction intensity (β = 4.552, p = 0.001) have positive significant effects that survive the controls and fixed effects, whereas usage rate has no significant independent effect; GDP per capita is the strongest control. Fintech advances inclusion through breadth of access and economically meaningful transaction use rather than frequency of use: repeated low-value transfers do not connect users to formal savings, credit or insurance. Because the effects reflect long-run co-movement rather than year-to-year changes, they are interpreted as long-run associations. Policy should prioritise affordable access, interoperable payments and bank–fintech partnerships that convert activity into formal participation. JEL classification numbers: G21, G23, O16, O33, O55. Keywords: Financial technology, Financial inclusion, Penetration rate, Usage rate, Transaction intensity, East African Community.

latest.title: Cross-Context Comparison of AI-Enabled CRM: Mechanisms, Challenges and Future Directions in B2B and B2C Settings
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping customer relationship management (CRM) in both business-tobusiness (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) contexts, yet the two settings differ markedly in relationship structure, decision-making processes, data characteristics and customer expectations. The core argument of this review is that AI-CRM exhibits significant contextual differences between B2B and B2C, with variations in its capability dimensions, action pathways, performance outcomes, and facilitating and hindering factors. Accordingly, firms cannot directly transfer AI-CRM strategies from one context to another; instead, they should adapt strategies based on differences in relationship structures, decision-making processes and customer expectations. By integrating existing literature, this paper systematically compares the mechanisms, performance outcomes and challenges of AICRM across B2B and B2C scenarios. The study finds that AI-CRM in the B2B context places greater emphasis on organizational capabilities, institutional support and process integration, while the B2C context focuses more on personalized experiences, emotional interaction and consumer trust. Both contexts face common challenges such as ethics, privacy and data bias, but differ in focus and response approaches. Existing research mostly examines B2B or B2C in isolation, lacking direct comparison. Future research should strengthen cross-context theoretical construction and empirical testing. Finally, this paper outlines the future research directions derived from the review.

latest.title: Applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Marketing: A Research Review and Future Prospects
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is turning marketing content into an abundant resource with near-zero marginal cost, but related research is highly fragmented. This paper thematically integrates Chinese- and English-language literature published from 2019 to 2026. The findings show that gains from GenAI marketing are “stratified along the funnel”: evidence of improvements at the attention and interaction stages is sufficient, whereas the effect on final conversion is weak; consumers’ evaluations of content are decoupled from evaluations of the “artificial intelligence (AI) source” label, and disclosure of the AI source significantly suppresses transactions; only 13% of the literature examines moderating variables. Accordingly, this paper proposes a five-stage integrated framework of “technical characteristics → marketing applications → psychological mechanisms → consumer responses → moderating boundaries” and a future research agenda.

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings.
